entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Zariski topology
entries.definition: Jointly surjective open immersions. On the finite-type site one can take finite families, including the empty cover of the empty scheme.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of local rings.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Nisnevich topology
entries.definition: Completely decomposed étale families: every target point has a lift whose induced residue-field map is an isomorphism.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of henselian local rings.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Étale topology
entries.definition: Jointly surjective étale families.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of strictly henselian local rings.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Smooth topology
entries.definition: Jointly surjective smooth families. Smooth surjections admit sections étale locally on the target, so their generated topology is already étale.
refs: Stacks 055U · étale-local sections of smooth morphisms
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of strictly henselian local rings (by equality with étale).

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Syntomic topology
entries.definition: Jointly surjective syntomic families. Syntomic means flat, locally of finite presentation, with local complete intersection geometric fibres.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Fppf topology
entries.definition: Jointly surjective flat morphisms locally of finite presentation. Over a locally Noetherian target, finite flat maps are finite locally free; in general use finite locally free maps in the generation theorem.
refs: Stacks 05WM · finite locally free refinements of fppf covers
Stacks 0DET · étale-local finite locally free refinement

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Fpqc topology
entries.definition: Flat families for which each affine open of the target is covered by images of finitely many quasi-compact opens in the sources that map into that affine open. In particular a faithfully flat quasi-compact morphism is a singleton cover.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Canonical topology
entries.definition: The finest topology for which every representable presheaf is a sheaf. A sieve covers precisely when it is universally effective epimorphic, tested by descent of maps into every object after each base change.
refs: Stacks 00WO · representable sheaves and the canonical topology
Stacks 00Z9 · finest topology making given presheaves sheaves

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Qfh topology
entries.definition: On the finite-type site one may take finite families of quasi-finite maps whose coproduct is a universal topological epimorphism (a quotient map after all base changes).
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of absolutely integrally closed local domains.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Closed topology
entries.definition: Finite jointly surjective families of closed immersions on the finite-type site.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of domains.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Completely decomposed finite topology
entries.definition: Finite families of finite maps with a residue-field-preserving lift of every point.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of normal domains.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Prime-to-ℓ finite flat topology
entries.definition: Fix a prime ℓ. Use singleton finite flat surjections of constant rank d with ℓ ∤ d. Such maps are finite locally free in the finite-type Noetherian setting.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Finite flat topology
entries.definition: Singleton finite flat surjections. In the Noetherian setting these are precisely finite locally free surjections.
refs: Stacks 05WM · finite locally free refinements of fppf covers

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Finite topology
entries.definition: Finite jointly surjective families of finite morphisms on the finite-type site.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of absolutely integrally closed domains.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Proper topology
entries.definition: Finite jointly surjective families of proper morphisms on the finite-type site.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Envelope topology
entries.definition: Finite families of proper morphisms with a residue-field-preserving lift of every point.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Rh topology
entries.definition: Generated by Zariski coverings and completely decomposed proper coverings.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of valuation rings.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Cdh topology
entries.definition: Generated by Nisnevich and rh covers, equivalently by Nisnevich and completely decomposed proper covers.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of henselian valuation rings.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: Eh topology
entries.definition: Generated by étale and rh covers, equivalently by étale and completely decomposed proper covers.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of strictly henselian valuation rings.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: ℓdh topology
entries.definition: Fix a prime ℓ. Adjoin prime-to-ℓ finite flat surjections to cdh covers.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of henselian valuation rings whose fraction fields have no nontrivial finite extension of degree prime to ℓ.

entries.subject: classical-cover
entries.ambient: Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.
entries.name: H topology
entries.definition: Generated by Zariski open covers and proper surjections on the finite-type site. Equivalently, use finite families whose coproduct is a universal topological epimorphism.
entries.points: For the Gabber–Kelly finite-type site, the affine local test objects are spectra of absolutely integrally closed valuation rings.

entries.subject: qcqs-cover
entries.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
entries.name: Fpqc topology
entries.definition: Use the fpqc families from the classical comparison, restricted to this category.
refs: Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph

entries.subject: qcqs-cover
entries.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
entries.name: Ph topology
entries.definition: Use Zariski covers and proper surjections as generators. The Stacks Project distinguishes ph from its finite-presentation h convention. Over the separated finite-type Noetherian site of the classical comparison these are the same generators used there for h.
refs: Stacks 0EVM · affine inverse limits of h and ph covers

entries.subject: qcqs-cover
entries.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
entries.name: Valuative (v) topology
entries.definition: For a map of qcqs schemes $Y\to X$, test every $\operatorname{Spec}V\to X$ for a valuation ring $V$. There must be an injective local map of valuation rings $V\hookrightarrow W$ and a lift $\operatorname{Spec}W\to Y$ over $X$. For families, work affine locally on the target and take finite affine refinements whose disjoint union passes the test.
refs: Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph
Stacks 0EVM · affine inverse limits of h and ph covers

entries.subject: qcqs-cover
entries.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
entries.name: Arc topology
entries.definition: Use the same lifting test but restrict both valuation rings $V$ and $W$ to rank at most one. Rank zero includes fields. For families use the corresponding affine-local finite refinement convention.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Local properties of a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$; the definitions are checked in neighbourhoods of source and target points.
entries.name: Locally of finite presentation
entries.definition: On affine charts the coordinate algebra is finitely presented over the target ring.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Local properties of a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$; the definitions are checked in neighbourhoods of source and target points.
entries.name: Locally of finite type
entries.definition: On affine charts the coordinate algebra is finitely generated over the target ring.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Local properties of a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$; the definitions are checked in neighbourhoods of source and target points.
entries.name: Étale
entries.definition: Smooth of relative dimension zero; equivalently flat, unramified and locally of finite presentation.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Local properties of a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$; the definitions are checked in neighbourhoods of source and target points.
entries.name: Smooth
entries.definition: Locally of finite presentation, flat, with geometrically regular fibres.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Local properties of a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$; the definitions are checked in neighbourhoods of source and target points.
entries.name: Syntomic
entries.definition: Flat, locally of finite presentation, and with geometric fibres that are local complete intersections.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Local properties of a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$; the definitions are checked in neighbourhoods of source and target points.
entries.name: Flat
entries.definition: For every $x\in X$ the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat over O at $f(x)$. Equivalently on affine charts, tensoring with the coordinate algebra is exact.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Local properties of a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$; the definitions are checked in neighbourhoods of source and target points.
entries.name: Unramified
entries.definition: Locally of finite type with zero relative differentials. Equivalently, the diagonal is an open immersion and the map is locally of finite type.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Local properties of a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$; the definitions are checked in neighbourhoods of source and target points.
entries.name: Local complete intersection
entries.definition: In the Stacks convention, locally factor as a Koszul-regular closed immersion followed by a smooth map. For locally Noetherian schemes this is the regular-sequence formulation.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of the local rings or of the underlying space of one scheme X.
entries.name: Locally Noetherian
entries.definition: Has an affine open covering with Noetherian coordinate rings. Requiring just Noetherian stalks is insufficient.

pibase.title: Noetherian space
pibase.note: A locally Noetherian scheme has a basis of Noetherian open subspaces. A Noetherian open subspace need not have a Noetherian structure sheaf.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of the local rings or of the underlying space of one scheme X.
entries.name: Locally connected
entries.definition: Every point has a basis of connected open neighbourhoods.

pibase.title: Locally connected
pibase.note: Apply the connected-open basis criterion to the underlying space of the scheme.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of the local rings or of the underlying space of one scheme X.
entries.name: Regular
entries.definition: Locally Noetherian and every local ring is regular: its dimension equals the minimal number of generators of its maximal ideal.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of the local rings or of the underlying space of one scheme X.
entries.name: Normal
entries.definition: Every local ring is an integrally closed domain. This definition does not assume the scheme locally Noetherian.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of the local rings or of the underlying space of one scheme X.
entries.name: Reduced
entries.definition: All stalks have zero nilradical; equivalently every affine coordinate ring is reduced.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of the local rings or of the underlying space of one scheme X.
entries.name: Local complete intersection
entries.definition: Locally Noetherian, with each local ring having completion isomorphic to a quotient of a regular local ring by a regular sequence.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of the local rings or of the underlying space of one scheme X.
entries.name: Gorenstein
entries.definition: Locally Noetherian, with each local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of the local rings or of the underlying space of one scheme X.
entries.name: Cohen–Macaulay
entries.definition: Locally Noetherian, with depth equal to Krull dimension at each local ring.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Affine
entries.definition: For every affine open V of Y, $f^{-1}(V)$ is affine.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Quasi-affine
entries.definition: A quasi-compact morphism for which each affine open of Y has quasi-affine inverse image. Equivalently, a quasi-compact open immersion into a scheme affine over Y.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Finite
entries.definition: Affine, with every corresponding coordinate algebra finite as a module over the base ring.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Projective
entries.definition: A closed subscheme of a projective bundle $\mathbb P_Y(\mathcal E)$ over Y for a quasi-coherent module E of finite type (Stacks convention). H-projective uses a fixed finite-dimensional projective space over Y.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Quasi-projective
entries.definition: Of finite type and admitting a relatively ample invertible sheaf, in the Stacks convention.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Quasi-compact
entries.definition: The inverse image of every quasi-compact open is quasi-compact; equivalently test affine opens of Y.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Proper
entries.definition: Separated, of finite type and universally closed.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Separated
entries.definition: The diagonal $X\to X\times_Y X$ is a closed immersion.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Quasi-separated
entries.definition: The diagonal $X\to X\times_Y X$ is quasi-compact.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Of finite type
entries.definition: Locally of finite type and quasi-compact.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: Properties of $f\colon X\to Y$ with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.
entries.name: Of finite presentation
entries.definition: Locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Irreducible
entries.definition: The space is nonempty and is not a union of two proper closed subsets. Equivalently every two nonempty opens intersect.

pibase.title: Hyperconnected (irreducible)
pibase.note: Apply the hyperconnected criterion to the underlying space, with the additional requirement that the scheme is nonempty.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Connected
entries.definition: The space admits no partition into two nonempty disjoint opens.

pibase.title: Connected
pibase.note: Apply the point-set definition to the underlying space of the scheme.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Local
entries.definition: A local scheme is $\operatorname{Spec} A$ for a local ring A. Equivalently, it has a unique closed point to which every point specializes.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Affine
entries.definition: Isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec} A$ for a ring A.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Quasi-affine
entries.definition: A quasi-compact scheme admitting an open immersion into an affine scheme.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Quasi-compact
entries.definition: Every open covering admits a finite subcover, with no separation axiom implied.

pibase.title: Compact (quasi-compact)
pibase.note: Scheme quasi-compactness is quasi-compactness of the underlying space; π-Base does not require Hausdorffness for “compact”.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Separated
entries.definition: Separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$; the diagonal into the product over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ is closed.

pibase.title: Hausdorff (T₂)
pibase.note: Scheme-separatedness tests a closed immersion into the scheme fibre product. It does not imply that the Zariski space is Hausdorff.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Quasi-separated
entries.definition: Intersections of any two affine opens are quasi-compact.

pibase.title: Spectral
pibase.note: For schemes, quasi-separatedness gives the finite-intersection condition on quasi-compact opens. Add quasi-compactness to conclude spectrality.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Noetherian
entries.definition: Has a finite open affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings.

pibase.title: Noetherian space
pibase.note: A Noetherian scheme has a Noetherian underlying space. The converse fails: a non-Noetherian local ring with just one prime ideal has a Noetherian spectrum.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Integral
entries.definition: Nonempty, reduced and irreducible; equivalently every nonempty affine open has a domain as coordinate ring.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.ambient: Properties of X itself. For separatedness, the base of the structure morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$.
entries.name: Spectral
entries.definition: Quasi-compact, sober, with a basis of quasi-compact opens stable under finite intersection. A scheme has spectral underlying space exactly when it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

pibase.title: Spectral
pibase.note: The original Zariski space satisfies the spectral axioms.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change $Y^{\prime}\to Y$.
entries.name: Flat ∧ locally finitely presented
entries.definition: Both flatness and local finite presentation hold for the same morphism.
refs: Stacks 01UA · flat morphisms locally of finite presentation are universally open

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change $Y^{\prime}\to Y$.
entries.name: Universally open
entries.definition: After every base change the map sends opens to opens.
refs: Stacks 01UA · flat morphisms locally of finite presentation are universally open

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change $Y^{\prime}\to Y$.
entries.name: Universal homeomorphism
entries.definition: Every base change is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces. No isomorphism of structure sheaves is required.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change $Y^{\prime}\to Y$.
entries.name: Universally closed
entries.definition: After every base change the map sends closed sets to closed sets.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change $Y^{\prime}\to Y$.
entries.name: Surjective
entries.definition: Every point of the target has a preimage. Surjectivity of schemes is preserved under arbitrary base change.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change $Y^{\prime}\to Y$.
entries.name: Universally injective
entries.definition: Injective after every base change. Equivalently injective on points with purely inseparable residue field extensions.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.ambient: A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change $Y^{\prime}\to Y$.
entries.name: Integral morphism
entries.definition: Affine, and integral on coordinate rings (every element satisfies a monic polynomial over the base).

entries.subject: scheme
entries.name: Qcqs scheme
entries.definition: The scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Equivalently, it has a finite affine open cover and intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact.
refs: Stacks 094L · the space of a qcqs scheme is spectral

pibase.title: Spectral
pibase.note: For schemes, qcqs is equivalent to spectrality of the underlying space. For general spaces, use the spectral axioms directly.

entries.subject: morphism
entries.name: Qcqs morphism
entries.definition: The morphism and its diagonal are quasi-compact. Equivalently, the morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.name: Krull dimension at most zero
entries.definition: Every point of the underlying space is closed. Equivalently, no affine chart has a strict inclusion of prime ideals. This convention includes the empty scheme.

pibase.title: T₁
pibase.note: Krull dimension at most zero is equivalent to all points of a scheme being closed.

pibase.title: Zero dimensional (clopen basis)
pibase.note: π-Base zero dimensionality is a clopen basis condition. It is weaker in general point-set topology; the two are equivalent for spectral spaces when combined with T₀, as in the scheme setting.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.name: Hausdorff underlying space
entries.definition: Any two distinct points have disjoint Zariski-open neighbourhoods.
refs: Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology

pibase.title: Hausdorff (T₂)
pibase.note: The separation axiom is imposed on the underlying Zariski space.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.name: Profinite underlying space
entries.definition: The underlying Zariski space is a cofiltered inverse limit of finite discrete spaces.

pibase.title: Stone space (profinite)
pibase.note: The original Zariski space, with its given topology, is a Stone space.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.name: Spectral with profinite patch topology
entries.definition: The Zariski space is spectral and its patch topology, generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements, is profinite.
refs: Stacks 094L · the space of a qcqs scheme is spectral
Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology

pibase.title: Stone space (profinite)
pibase.note: Apply Stone space to the patch topology, not to the original spectral topology.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Quasi-compact space
entries.definition: Every open cover admits a finite subcover.

pibase.title: Compact (quasi-compact)
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Hausdorff space
entries.definition: Distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods.

pibase.title: Hausdorff (T₂)
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Totally disconnected space
entries.definition: Each nonempty connected component consists of a single point.

pibase.title: Totally disconnected
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Profinite space
entries.definition: A cofiltered inverse limit of finite discrete spaces. Equivalently, quasi-compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected.

pibase.title: Stone space (profinite)
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Spectral space
entries.definition: A sober, quasi-compact space with a basis of quasi-compact opens and with their pairwise intersections quasi-compact.
refs: Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology

pibase.title: Spectral
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: T₁ space
entries.definition: Every singleton is closed.
refs: Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology

pibase.title: T₁
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Sober space
entries.definition: Every nonempty irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point.
refs: Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology

pibase.title: Sober
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Qc Zariski basis site
entries.definition: For a qcqs scheme X, take its quasi-compact open subsets, with inclusions as arrows and finite open covers as covering families. Intersections stay in the basis, and restriction identifies Zariski sheaves with sheaves on this site.
refs: Stacks 0069 · quasi-compact opens and finite refinements

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Qc topology on locally quasi-compact spaces
entries.definition: Objects are locally quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces and maps are continuous. A family covers if every target point has a neighbourhood that is the union of images of finitely many quasi-compact subsets of the sources, in the sense that the union contains an open neighbourhood of the point.
refs: Stacks 09WY · the qc topology and comparison with open covers

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Profinite site for condensed sets
entries.definition: On a size-bounded category of profinite spaces, covers are finite families of jointly surjective continuous maps. With the strong limit size convention of the cited lectures, sheaves of sets are the corresponding condensed sets.

pibase.title: Stone space (profinite)
pibase.note: The objects satisfy this point-set property; the site adds a class of covering families.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Constructible topology
entries.definition: On a spectral space take the topology generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements. The identity to the original spectral space is continuous. The topology is profinite and equals the original one exactly when the original is Hausdorff.
refs: Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology

pibase.title: Stone space (profinite)
pibase.note: The patch topology of a spectral space is profinite, hence defines a Stone space.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Grothendieck site
entries.ambient: A category in a fixed size convention
entries.definition: A category equipped with a Grothendieck topology: covering sieves contain the maximal sieve, are stable under pullback and satisfy local character. A site is a presentation; equivalent categories of sheaves can arise from different sites.
refs: Stacks 00Z4 · topology in terms of covering sieves
Stacks 00ZC · passage from a site to a topology

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Grothendieck topos
entries.ambient: Sheaves of sets
entries.definition: A category equivalent to sheaves of sets on a small site. A geometric morphism is an adjoint pair with left exact inverse image. A point is a geometric morphism from Set; a site need not be recoverable from its topos.
refs: Stacks 00XA · topos and morphisms of topoi

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Ringed topos
entries.ambient: Grothendieck topoi
entries.definition: A topos with a sheaf of rings as structure sheaf. Sheaves of modules, and their derived global sections, depend on this extra structure.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: ∞-topos
entries.ambient: ∞-categories in a fixed universe
entries.definition: An ∞-category $\mathcal X$ is an ∞-topos if there is a small ∞-category $\mathcal C$ and an accessible left exact localization $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal X$ of its presheaves of spaces.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Canonical Grothendieck topology
entries.ambient: A small category C in the chosen universe
entries.definition: The canonical topology $J_{\mathrm{can}}$ on $\mathcal C$ is the largest Grothendieck topology on $\mathcal C$ for which every representable presheaf is a sheaf.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Petit Zariski site
entries.ambient: Open subsets of a scheme X
entries.definition: Objects are opens, arrows are inclusions and coverings are ordinary open covers. Its sheaves are the usual sheaves on the underlying Zariski space.
refs: Blechschmidt, Using the internal language of toposes in algebraic geometry, Parts II–III
Stacks 020T · big and small Zariski sites
Stacks 020X · small Zariski site and usual topology

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Gros Zariski site
entries.ambient: Size bounded category of schemes over S
entries.definition: Arrows are S-morphisms. A covering family consists of open immersions with images covering the target. This is a different presentation and category from the open subsets of S.
refs: Blechschmidt, Using the internal language of toposes in algebraic geometry, Parts II–III
Stacks 020T · big and small Zariski sites

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Affine finite presentation Zariski site
entries.ambient: Opposite of finitely presented R-algebras
entries.definition: Finite families of principal localizations at elements generating the unit ideal form a basis for the topology. This is the restricted big affine presentation over Spec R used in the thesis, with its stated size conventions.
refs: Blechschmidt, Using the internal language of toposes in algebraic geometry, Parts II–III

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Petit étale site
entries.ambient: Étale schemes over X, within a fixed size convention
entries.definition: Objects are étale maps to X and covers are jointly surjective étale families. A geometric point gives the stalk defined by the filtered system of pointed étale neighbourhoods.
refs: Stacks 021B · big and small étale sites

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Gros étale site
entries.ambient: Size bounded category of schemes over X
entries.definition: Objects are arbitrary X-schemes in the chosen category; covers are jointly surjective étale families. The covering condition is shared with the small étale site, but the objects differ.
refs: Stacks 040S · geometric points on the big site

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Petit Nisnevich site
entries.ambient: Étale schemes over X
entries.definition: An étale family covers if every target point lifts to a point inducing an isomorphism of residue fields. Joint surjectivity alone does not give this condition.
refs: Voevodsky, Unstable motivic homotopy categories in Nisnevich and cdh-topologies
Nisnevich, The completely decomposed topology on schemes

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Scheme pro-étale site
entries.ambient: Weakly étale schemes over X, in the Stacks convention
entries.definition: Weakly étale means that the map and its diagonal are flat. Use the fpqc covering condition on weakly étale objects, including the finite quasi-compact refinement condition; joint surjectivity alone is insufficient in general.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-étale topology for schemes, §4
Stacks 098K · big and small pro-étale sites

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Étale site of an algebraic space
entries.ambient: Schemes étale over an algebraic space X
entries.definition: Use scheme charts étale over X and jointly surjective étale covering families. Allowing algebraic spaces as objects gives an equivalent topos by the special cocontinuous comparison.
refs: Stacks 03ED · small étale site of an algebraic space
Stacks 03G1 · comparison with algebraic spaces as objects
Stacks 0H01 · affine étale site of an algebraic space

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Lisse-étale site
entries.ambient: Schemes smooth over an algebraic stack
entries.definition: Objects are smooth maps from schemes, with the usual triangles up to a specified 2-isomorphism; covers are jointly surjective étale families. Arbitrary maps of algebraic stacks do not in general induce morphisms of their lisse-étale topoi.
refs: Stacks 0787 · definition of the lisse-étale and flat-fppf sites

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Flat-fppf site
entries.ambient: Schemes flat over an algebraic stack
entries.definition: Objects are flat scheme maps to the stack. Covering arrows form an fppf family of the source schemes, so they are flat and locally of finite presentation.
refs: Stacks 0787 · definition of the flat-fppf site
Stacks 0787 · definition of the lisse-étale and flat-fppf sites

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Big fppf site of an algebraic stack
entries.ambient: A category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of schemes
entries.definition: Covering families are those whose projected family is fppf. The ambient fibred category also inherits the Zariski, étale, smooth and syntomic topologies.
refs: Stacks 06NV · inherited topology on a fibred category

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Small crystalline site
entries.ambient: PD base (S,I,γ) and a scheme X over V(I), with Stacks hypotheses
entries.definition: An object is an open U of X and a compatible divided power thickening U ↪ T over S (including the local nilpotence condition on p in the cited setup). Covers are induced by open covers of T and restriction of the thickening.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Big crystalline site
entries.ambient: PD base (S,I,γ) and a scheme X over V(I), with Stacks hypotheses
entries.definition: Use compatible divided power thickenings U ↪ T over S with a map U → X; U need not be open in X. Covers are induced by open covers of T, with U pulled back.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Crystal on a crystalline site
entries.ambient: Modules over the crystalline structure sheaf
entries.definition: The structure sheaf takes sections of the thickening T. A crystal has invertible pullback comparison maps on every morphism of thickenings. This condition is extra structure on a sheaf of modules, not a topology.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Prism
entries.ambient: δ-rings at a prime p
entries.definition: A prism is a δ-ring A with an ideal I defining an effective Cartier divisor, such that A is derived (p,I)-complete and $p\in I+\varphi(I)A$.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Relative prismatic site
entries.ambient: A bounded base prism (A,I) and a p-adic formal A/I-scheme X
entries.definition: Use bounded prisms (B,IB) over (A,I) equipped with a map Spf(B/IB) → X. Covers are generated by maps induced by (p,I)-completely faithfully flat extensions of prism rings, with arrows viewed opposite to the ring maps.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Absolute prismatic site
entries.ambient: p-adic formal scheme X
entries.definition: In the bounded convention, use bounded prisms (A,I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, without choosing a base prism. Covers are generated by (p,I)-completely faithfully flat maps of prism rings, with the opposite site orientation.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prismatic F-crystals and crystalline Galois representations, §2

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Quasisyntomic site
entries.ambient: Opposite of the category of quasisyntomic rings
entries.definition: An object is a p-complete ring A with bounded p-power torsion and $L_{A/\mathbf Z_p}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A/pA$ of Tor amplitude [-1,0] over A/pA. Covers are p-completely faithfully flat quasisyntomic maps.
refs: Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, Topological Hochschild homology and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Definitions 1.7 and 4.10

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Infinitesimal site
entries.ambient: Scheme X over S
entries.definition: In the small formulation use open U of X and nilpotent thickenings U ↪ T over S with coverings induced by opens of T. There are no divided powers in this definition.
refs: Hartshorne, On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Kummer étale site
entries.ambient: Fine saturated log schemes over a fixed fs log scheme
entries.definition: Kummer log étale maps give coverings when their underlying maps are jointly surjective. The Kummer condition is imposed on characteristic monoids at geometric points.
refs: Illusie, Kummer étale cohomology and log blow-up invariance

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Kummer flat site
entries.ambient: Fine saturated log schemes over a fixed fs log scheme
entries.definition: Use jointly surjective Kummer log flat covering families with the finite presentation condition in Kato’s convention. Pullbacks are in the fs category, which may require saturation.
refs: Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine–Illusie II

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Full log étale site
entries.ambient: Fine saturated log schemes
entries.definition: Uses log étale morphisms in Nakayama’s full logarithmic site, which incorporates log modifications and is distinct from the Kummer étale site. The cover definition and use of the fs fibre product are as in the cited paper.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Complex analytic topology
entries.ambient: Analytification of a locally finite type complex scheme
entries.definition: On affine finite type charts use the Euclidean topology on the complex zero set; glue along open charts. The resulting site uses ordinary open subsets of the analytification.
refs: Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Rigid analytic admissible G-topology
entries.ambient: Rigid analytic spaces in the sense of Tate
entries.definition: The site uses admissible open subspaces and admissible coverings. On affinoids the admissible cover condition is tested using finite affinoid refinements; arbitrary unions of point sets do not supply the cover condition.
refs: Conrad, Several approaches to non-archimedean geometry

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Rigid analytic pro-étale site
entries.ambient: Locally Noetherian adic spaces in Scholze’s framework
entries.definition: The site uses pro-étale objects obtained locally from inverse systems of étale objects with eventual finite étale transition maps, using the coverings of Scholze §3. This is distinct from the weakly étale scheme site.
refs: Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Étale site of a locally spatial diamond
entries.ambient: Étale maps of diamonds to X
entries.definition: Covers are jointly surjective étale families. For an analytic adic space in Scholze’s construction, the associated diamond has the equivalent étale site described in §15.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Quasi-pro-étale site of a diamond
entries.ambient: Locally spatial diamonds quasi-pro-étale over X
entries.definition: The quasi-pro-étale condition is tested after pulling back to strictly totally disconnected perfectoid spaces. The cover families are the v-covering families between the selected objects.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Perfectoid v-site
entries.ambient: Perfectoid spaces (for diamonds, in characteristic p)
entries.definition: A family covers if each quasi-compact open of the target can be covered by images of finitely many quasi-compact opens in its sources. The site is used for diamonds and v-sheaves; it does not share the underlying category of the scheme v-site.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Adic tame site
entries.ambient: Adic spaces in Hübner’s setting
entries.definition: A variant of the étale site with the tameness of the induced extensions of residue valuations built into the morphisms. Its role and comparison with étale cohomology are developed in the cited construction.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Relative tame site of schemes
entries.ambient: Scheme X over a base S with S-valuations
entries.definition: Use étale objects and require, in addition to covering points, tame lifts of the valuations in the relative sense. The definition depends on the chosen base, and the test is stronger than joint surjectivity.
refs: Hübner–Schmidt, The tame site of a scheme

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Cdarc topology
entries.ambient: Qcqs schemes in the motivic excision setting
entries.definition: Completely decomposed analogue of the arc topology. Use the lifting condition against rank at most one valuation rings specified in the cited definition; the complete decomposition condition is essential.
refs: Elmanto–Hoyois–Iwasa–Kelly, Cdh descent, cdarc descent, and Milnor excision

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Motivic Nisnevich presentation
entries.ambient: Smooth schemes over a base S
entries.definition: Start from Nisnevich sheaves of spaces and impose A¹-invariance by localization at the projections X × A¹ → X. This localization is additional to the sheaf condition.
refs: Voevodsky, Unstable motivic homotopy categories in Nisnevich and cdh-topologies

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Derived étale site
entries.ambient: Opposite category of connective derived commutative rings, or relative version
entries.definition: In the connective setting an étale map has étale π₀ and the higher homotopy groups are obtained by base change along π₀. A covering family is detected by joint surjectivity on the ordinary spectra. Use the chosen derived ring model and sheaves of spaces.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Spectral étale site
entries.ambient: Opposite category of connective E∞-rings, or relative version
entries.definition: Étaleness is characterized by étale π₀ and base change for the homotopy groups; covers are detected on ordinary spectra of π₀. Spectral here refers to ring spectra, a different usage from Hochster’s spectral spaces.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Derived fppf topology
entries.ambient: Derived affine schemes in the connective convention
entries.definition: Use flat locally finitely presented morphisms, with flatness detected by π₀ flatness and base change on higher homotopy, and joint surjectivity on ordinary spectra. This uses homotopical descent, not just set-valued gluing.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Locale
entries.ambient: Point-free topology
entries.definition: The category of locales is the opposite of the category of frames. A map of locales is specified contravariantly by the inverse-image homomorphism of their frames of opens.
refs: Blechschmidt, Generalized spaces for constructive algebra
The patch topology in univalent foundations

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Coherent locale
entries.ambient: Point-free topology
entries.definition: Its frame is generated by compact elements closed under finite meets and containing the top. Equivalently the frame is the ideal completion of its bounded distributive lattice of compact elements.
refs: Blechschmidt, Generalized spaces for constructive algebra
The patch topology in univalent foundations
Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings (1969)

pibase.title: Spectral
pibase.note: Classical coherent locale duality relates these objects to spectral spaces; the point-free presentation is kept separate.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Hochster dual topology
entries.ambient: A spectral space X
entries.definition: Use complements of quasi-compact open subsets of X as a basis. Duality reverses specialization, is involutive on spectral spaces and does not change the patch topology.
refs: Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings (1969)
Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Spectral map
entries.ambient: Continuous maps of spectral spaces
entries.definition: Inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. The corresponding pullback on bounded distributive lattices preserves finite joins and meets.
refs: Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings (1969)
Stacks 08YG · spectral spaces and spectral maps

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Petit fppf site
entries.ambient: Schemes flat and locally of finite presentation over X
entries.definition: Objects are the indicated X-schemes in the chosen size bound; families cover by jointly surjective flat maps locally of finite presentation. The qualifier fppf applies both to the objects over X and to the arrows in covering families.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Finite étale site
entries.ambient: Schemes finite étale over X
entries.definition: Use jointly surjective covering families among the finite étale objects over X. Over a connected pointed scheme their fibre functor gives a Galois category, which determines the profinite étale fundamental group.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Finite presentation h topology
entries.ambient: Schemes over a base in the Stacks Project convention
entries.definition: Covering sieves admit, locally on affine opens of the target, refinement by finite affine covers of a proper surjection of finite presentation. This separates the finite presentation h convention from ph, which uses proper surjections without the finite presentation hypothesis.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Pro-Nisnevich site
entries.ambient: Mattis’s category of pro-smooth schemes over S
entries.definition: Covering families are pro-étale, fpqc, and completely decomposed on their disjoint union: every target point lifts with unchanged residue field. The paper compares the resulting ∞-topos with the smooth Nisnevich ∞-topos.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Pro-cdh site on schemes
entries.ambient: Finite presentation schemes over a qcqs base S
entries.definition: Generate the topology by distinguished Nisnevich covers and pro-abstract blowup covers. For a proper map that is an isomorphism off a finitely presented closed subscheme, the latter family includes the proper map and all infinitesimal thickenings of the center.
refs: Kelly–Saito, A procdh topology, Definitions 1.1 and 2.1

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Pro-cdh site on formal schemes
entries.ambient: Formal schemes in the finite-type category specified by Kelly and Saito
entries.definition: Use Nisnevich covers and formal abstract blowup covers. This presentation uses the formal completion at a center in the formal scheme category; the pro-cdh site on ordinary schemes uses the family of its finite thickenings.
refs: Kelly–Saito, A pro-cdh topology on formal schemes

entries.subject: site
entries.name: p-complete arc site
entries.ambient: Opposite of the category of derived p-complete commutative rings
entries.definition: A singleton cover passes the arc lifting test against p-complete valuation rings of rank at most one, with extensions also p-complete and of rank at most one. Mathew distinguishes this from the variant testing rank one and requiring p to be nonzero.
refs: Mathew, On K(1)-local TR, Definitions 1.6 and 7.1

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Huber adic spectrum topology
entries.ambient: An adic spectrum Spa(A,A⁺) of a Huber pair
entries.definition: Points are continuous valuations up to equivalence that are at most 1 on A⁺. Rational subsets, specified by finitely many inequalities $|f_i|\le |g|\ne0$ with the open-ideal condition, form a basis of quasi-compact opens. The adic spectrum is spectral.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Berkovich spectrum topology
entries.ambient: Berkovich spectrum of a non-Archimedean affinoid algebra A
entries.definition: Points are bounded multiplicative seminorms with the prescribed restriction to the base field. The topology is initial for the evaluations $x\mapsto |f(x)|$ with f in A. This ordinary point-set topology is distinct from the rigid admissible site.
refs: Berkovich, Spectral Theory and Analytic Geometry over Non-Archimedean Fields
Temkin, Introduction to Berkovich analytic spaces

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Spectral Zariski site
entries.ambient: Opposite of connective E∞-rings, or relative version
entries.definition: Basic opens of an affine spectral scheme come from inverting elements of π₀. A family of such localizations covers when the corresponding basic opens cover the ordinary spectrum of π₀.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: T₀ space
entries.definition: Distinct points are distinguished by some open subset. Equivalently, distinct points have distinct closures.

pibase.title: T₀
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Connected space
entries.definition: There is no cover by two disjoint nonempty open subsets.

pibase.title: Connected
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Hyperconnected space
entries.definition: Any two nonempty open subsets intersect. This includes the empty space; irreducibility of schemes adds nonemptiness.
refs: Stacks 004U · irreducible spaces and generic points

pibase.title: Hyperconnected (irreducible)
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Locally connected space
entries.definition: Connected open subsets form a basis of the topology.

pibase.title: Locally connected
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Noetherian topological space
entries.definition: The descending chain condition holds for closed subsets. Equivalently, every subspace is quasi-compact: the ascending chain condition on opens is equivalent to finite generation of their open unions.

pibase.title: Noetherian space
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Clopen basis (point-set zero dimensionality)
entries.definition: The topology has a basis of subsets that are both open and closed. This condition by itself imposes no separation axiom.

pibase.title: Zero dimensional (clopen basis)
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Extremally disconnected space
entries.definition: The closure of every open subset is open. The property is stronger than a clopen basis among profinite spaces, and is not the same as total disconnectedness.

pibase.title: Extremally disconnected
pibase.note: The two records describe the same property of a topological space.

entries.subject: scheme
entries.name: Noetherian underlying space
entries.definition: The Zariski space is Noetherian as a topological space. This condition alone does not require any affine coordinate ring to be Noetherian.
refs: Stacks 01OZ · Noetherian schemes have Noetherian spaces

pibase.title: Noetherian space
pibase.note: The descending chain condition is imposed on closed subsets of the underlying space.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Relative prismatic cohomology
entries.definition: $R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)=R\Gamma((X/A)_\Delta,\mathcal O_\Delta)$, where the structure sheaf evaluates to the prism ring. The complex has a semilinear Frobenius.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Definition 4.1 and Theorem 1.8

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Crystalline cohomology
entries.definition: The derived global sections of $\mathcal O_{X/S}$ on the small crystalline site. For a formal divided-power base in the prismatic comparison, use the $p$-adic crystalline theory of Bhatt–Scholze.
refs: Stacks 07IG · definition of the small crystalline site
Stacks 07IN · sheaves and the crystalline structure sheaf
Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorem 5.2

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Hodge–Tate differential forms
entries.definition: For $X=\operatorname{Spf}(R)$ smooth over a bounded prism quotient $A/I$, take the $p$-completed modules of differentials $\widehat{\Omega}^i_{R/(A/I)}\{-i\}$. The twist uses the invertible $A/I$-module $I/I^2$.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorems 1.8(2) and 6.3

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Completed relative de Rham cohomology
entries.definition: For smooth $p$-adic formal $X$ over $A/I$, take derived global sections of the relative $p$-completed de Rham complex.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorem 1.8(3) and Corollary 15.4

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Étale cohomology of the generic fibre
entries.definition: For the generic fibre $X_\eta$ of $X$ in the sense of Bhatt–Scholze, use $R\Gamma_{\acute{e}t}(X_\eta,\mathbf Z/p^n)$ with finite coefficients.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorems 1.8(4) and 9.1

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Locally finitely presented big Zariski site
entries.definition: Objects are schemes locally of finite presentation over the chosen base scheme. Covers are jointly surjective families of open immersions.
refs: Blechschmidt, Using the internal language of toposes, §15

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Bounded distributive lattice
entries.definition: A lattice with least and greatest elements and distributive finite meets and joins. Its ideal completion is a coherent frame. Its prime spectrum carries the basic opens consisting of prime ideals missing a given element.
refs: Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, Theorem 6
Blechschmidt, Generalized spaces for constructive algebra

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Prime spectrum of a ring
entries.definition: For a commutative ring $A$, the points of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ are prime ideals. The principal opens $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ form a basis of the Zariski topology.
refs: Stacks 00DY · the spectrum of a ring
Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, Theorem 6

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Big fppf site
entries.definition: Take a size-bounded category of schemes over a base scheme X. A family covers when its maps are flat and locally of finite presentation and their images jointly cover the target.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Formal small étale site
entries.definition: For a p-adic formal scheme X, use étale formal schemes over X and jointly surjective étale covers. Reduction identifies the site with the small étale site of the special fibre.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Construction 4.4
Stacks 0DE9 · §87.34, the small étale site of a formal algebraic space

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Localic topos
entries.definition: The topos of sheaves on a locale. In the frame presentation the objects are opens, arrows are inclusions, and a family covers an open when its join is that open.
refs: Blechschmidt, Generalized spaces for constructive algebra

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Covering-family presentation
entries.definition: A category with specified families of arrows $\{U_i\to U\}$ containing the isomorphism covers, closed under composition of covers, and stable under base change along every arrow to a covering target. The requisite pullbacks of the covering arrows exist.
refs: Stacks 00VH · site specified by covering families

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Sieve on an object
entries.definition: A sieve on $U$ is a subpresheaf $S\subseteq h_U$ of the representable presheaf. Equivalently its arrows with target $U$ are closed under precomposition. The pullback along $V\to U$ is $S\times_{h_U}h_V\subseteq h_V$.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Grothendieck topology in sieves
entries.definition: For each object $U$ choose a collection $J(U)$ of covering sieves. It contains $h_U$ and is stable under pullback. If $S\in J(U)$ and a sieve $R$ restricts to a covering sieve along every arrow in $S$, then $R\in J(U)$. A sheaf $F$ satisfies $F(U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(S,F)$ by restriction for each $S\in J(U)$.
refs: Stacks 00Z8 · sheaf condition for covering sieves

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Sheafification
entries.definition: The left adjoint $F\mapsto F^\#$ to the inclusion of sheaves of sets in presheaves. It can be computed by applying the plus construction twice. The plus construction forms the colimit, over refinements, of matching families on covers.
refs: Stacks 00ZM · sheafification for a topology in sieves

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Subcanonical topology
entries.definition: A Grothendieck topology $J$ on $\mathcal C$ is subcanonical if, for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, the representable presheaf $h_U$ is a $J$-sheaf.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Geometric morphism
entries.definition: A morphism $f:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ of topoi is an adjunction $f^{-1}:\mathcal F\rightleftarrows\mathcal E:f_*$ with $f^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. A point of $\mathcal E$ is a geometric morphism $\mathrm{Set}\to\mathcal E$.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Enough points
entries.definition: A family of points is conservative if a map of sheaves is an isomorphism whenever the induced map at every stalk in the family is bijective. A site has enough points when it admits a conservative family of points.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Weakly contractible object of a site
entries.definition: An object $U$ is weakly contractible if evaluation at $U$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections. Equivalently the canonical map $\coprod_i h_{U_i}^\#\to h_U^\#$ in sheaves admits a section for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}$.
refs: Stacks 090K · equivalent criteria for weak contractibility

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Big affine fppf site of a scheme
entries.definition: Take the full subcategory of the big fppf site over $S$ on those $U\to S$ for which $U$ is affine. Use finite jointly surjective families of flat, locally finitely presented morphisms from affine schemes as standard fppf covers.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Hypercompletion
entries.ambient: An ∞-topos
entries.definition: For an ∞-topos $\mathcal X$, form the accessible left exact localization at its ∞-connective morphisms. The resulting full reflective subcategory $\mathcal X^\wedge$ consists of objects local with respect to those morphisms.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Hypercomplete object
entries.ambient: Objects of an ∞-topos
entries.definition: An object $Z$ is hypercomplete if for every ∞-connective morphism $f:A\to B$, precomposition gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Hypercomplete ∞-topos
entries.ambient: ∞-topoi
entries.definition: An ∞-topos $\mathcal X$ is hypercomplete if every ∞-connective morphism in $\mathcal X$ is an equivalence.

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Hypercover
entries.ambient: Simplicial objects in a slice ∞-topos
entries.definition: A simplicial object $U_\bullet$ in $\mathcal X_{/V}$ is a hypercover of $V$ when for each $n\geq0$ the map $U_n\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{n-1}U_\bullet)_n$ is an effective epimorphism in the slice. In degree zero the matching object is the terminal object $V$ of the slice.
refs: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Definition 6.5.3.2, applied in the slice

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Effective hypercover
entries.ambient: Hypercovers in a slice ∞-topos
entries.definition: A hypercover $U_\bullet$ of $V$ is effective if its colimit in $\mathcal X_{/V}$ is terminal; equivalently the augmentation induces an equivalence $|U_\bullet|\simeq V$ in $\mathcal X$.
refs: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Definition 6.5.3.2, applied in the slice

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Bounded prism
entries.ambient: Prisms at a fixed prime p
entries.definition: A prism $(A,I)$ is bounded if there is an integer $n\geq0$ such that $p^n(A/I)[p^\infty]=0$.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Definition 1.1

entries.subject: site
entries.name: Frame
entries.ambient: Complete lattices
entries.definition: A frame is a complete lattice in which finite meets distribute over arbitrary joins. Frame homomorphisms preserve finite meets and arbitrary joins.
refs: Banaschewski, Radical ideals and coherent frames, §1

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Locally Noetherian space
entries.definition: Every point has a neighbourhood whose subspace topology is Noetherian. The neighbourhood is required to contain an open neighbourhood of the point.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Finitely many irreducible components
entries.definition: The set of maximal nonempty irreducible closed subsets of the space is finite.

entries.subject: space
entries.name: Every irreducible component has nonempty interior
entries.definition: For each maximal nonempty irreducible closed subset, its interior in the ambient space is nonempty.

entries.subject: algebraic-space
entries.name: Separated algebraic space
entries.definition: Take the absolute diagonal $\Delta_X:X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z} X$. It is a closed immersion.

entries.subject: algebraic-space
entries.name: Locally separated algebraic space
entries.definition: Take the absolute diagonal $\Delta_X:X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z} X$. It is an immersion.

entries.subject: algebraic-space
entries.name: Quasi-separated algebraic space
entries.definition: Take the absolute diagonal $\Delta_X:X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z} X$. It is quasi-compact.

entries.subject: algebraic-space
entries.name: Zariski locally quasi-separated algebraic space
entries.definition: There is a Zariski open cover by quasi-separated algebraic spaces.

entries.subject: algebraic-space
entries.name: Quasi-compact fibre products of affine tests
entries.definition: For every pair of morphisms $U\to X$ and $V\to X$ from affine schemes, the scheme $U\times_XV$ is quasi-compact.

entries.subject: algebraic-space
entries.name: Quasi-compact fibre products of quasi-compact tests
entries.definition: For every pair of morphisms $U\to X$ and $V\to X$ from quasi-compact schemes, the scheme $U\times_XV$ is quasi-compact.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Nonzero ring
entries.definition: The identities $0$ and $1$ are distinct.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Field
entries.definition: The ring is nonzero and every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Integral domain
entries.definition: The ring is nonzero and a product of two nonzero elements is nonzero.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Reduced ring
entries.definition: An element whose positive power is zero must itself be zero.
refs: Stacks 00EU · localization at a minimal prime
Stacks 00EW · embedding in products of fields

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Local ring
entries.definition: The ring has exactly one maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 07BI · local ring, residue field and local homomorphism

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Semilocal ring
entries.definition: The set of maximal ideals of the ring is finite.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Connected prime spectrum
entries.definition: The Zariski space $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is connected. Equivalently the only idempotents of $R$ are $0$ and $1$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Jacobson ring
entries.definition: Each radical ideal is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it.
refs: Stacks 00G2 · prime-ideal criterion for Jacobson rings

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Nilpotent nilradical
entries.definition: Some positive power of the ideal of all nilpotent elements vanishes.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Nilpotent Jacobson radical
entries.definition: Some positive power of the intersection of all maximal ideals vanishes.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Absolutely flat ring
entries.definition: Every module over the ring is flat.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Weak dimension at most one
entries.definition: Every module over the ring has flat dimension at most one. Equivalently, every ideal of the ring is flat as a module.
refs: Stacks 092S · characterizations of weak dimension at most one

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Field at every prime
entries.definition: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$, the local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Valuation ring at every prime
entries.definition: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$, the local ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a valuation ring.
refs: Stacks 092S · characterizations of weak dimension at most one

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Noetherian ring
entries.definition: Every ideal is finitely generated. Equivalently, every ascending chain of ideals stabilizes.
refs: Stacks 00B4 · Noetherian rings in the basic notions

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Artinian ring
entries.definition: Every descending chain of ideals stabilizes.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite length over itself
entries.definition: The ring as a module over itself has a finite composition series. The zero module has length zero.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Coherent ring
entries.definition: Every finitely generated ideal is a finitely presented module over the ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finitely many minimal primes
entries.definition: The set of prime ideals minimal under inclusion is finite.
refs: Stacks 00FR · Noetherian rings have finitely many minimal primes

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finitely many prime ideals
entries.definition: The underlying set of the prime spectrum is finite.
refs: Stacks 0ALV · finite prime spectrum of a Noetherian ring

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Krull dimension at most zero
entries.definition: There are no strict inclusions between prime ideals. Equivalently every prime ideal is maximal. This condition holds for the zero ring.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Krull dimension zero with nonempty spectrum
entries.definition: There exists at least one prime ideal and every prime ideal is maximal. This predicate explicitly requires nonzeroness.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Krull dimension at most one
entries.definition: No chain of prime ideals contains two consecutive strict inclusions.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Krull dimension exactly one
entries.definition: Prime chains have at most one strict inclusion, and a strict inclusion of prime ideals occurs.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite Krull dimension
entries.definition: A finite integer bounds the lengths of chains of strict prime-ideal inclusions.
refs: Stacks 00KG · Krull dimension and prime heights

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite global dimension
entries.definition: There is a finite bound on the projective dimensions of all modules over the ring.
refs: Stacks 00OE · finite global dimension and finite dimensional regularity

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite injective dimension over itself
entries.definition: The ring as a module over itself has a finite-length injective resolution.
refs: Stacks 0HB2 · finite injective dimension and Gorenstein rings

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Catenary ring
entries.definition: For each pair of nested primes there is a finite bound on chain lengths between them, and all maximal chains between them have the same length.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Universally catenary ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and every algebra of finite type over it is catenary.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Normal ring
entries.definition: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$, the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is an integrally closed domain.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Normal domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and is integrally closed in its fraction field.
refs: Stacks 030B · locality of normality for domains

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Integrally closed in the total ring of fractions
entries.definition: Each element of $Q(R)$ satisfying a monic polynomial over $R$ belongs to $R$. Here $Q(R)$ inverts all nonzerodivisors.
refs: Stacks 034M · normal rings are integrally closed in their total ring of fractions
Stacks 030C · criterion for reduced rings with finitely many minimal primes

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite product of normal domains
entries.definition: The ring is isomorphic to a finite product of normal domains. The empty product is the zero ring.
refs: Stacks 030C · product decomposition of normal rings with finitely many minimal primes

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Finite product of fields
entries.definition: The ring is isomorphic to a finite product of fields. The empty product is the zero ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Valuation ring
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and, in its fraction field, at least one of $x$ and $x^{-1}$ belongs to the ring for each nonzero $x$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Domination of local subrings
entries.definition: For local subrings A and B of a common field, B dominates A if A is contained in B and the maximal ideal of B contracts to that of A.
entries.ambient: The inclusion of local subrings of a common field.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Valuation ring centered on a subring
entries.definition: For a valuation ring A and a subring R of its fraction field, A is centered on R in the Stacks sense if A contains R.
refs: Stacks 00I9 · valuation ring centered on a subring
entries.ambient: An inclusion into the fraction field of a specified valuation ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Every finitely generated ideal is principal
entries.definition: Each finitely generated ideal can be generated by one element.
refs: Stacks 090Q · valuation-ring criterion in a local domain

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Every ideal is principal
entries.definition: For each ideal $I$ there is an element $a$ with $I=(a)$. Zero divisors are allowed.
refs: Stacks 034U · the principal-ideal condition in the definition of PID

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Every prime ideal is principal
entries.definition: Each prime ideal is generated by one element.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Every height-one prime is principal
entries.definition: Every prime ideal of height one is generated by one element.
refs: Stacks 0AFT · height-one criterion for a Noetherian domain to be a UFD

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Unique factorization domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain. Each nonzero nonunit factors into irreducibles, uniquely up to a permutation and replacement by associates.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Principal ideal domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and every ideal is principal.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Euclidean domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain with a natural-number-valued Euclidean function on its nonzero elements. Division by a nonzero element has remainder zero or a remainder of strictly smaller value than the divisor.
refs: Stacks 00B6 · Euclidean domain in basic notions

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Discrete valuation ring
entries.definition: The ring is the valuation ring of a surjective valuation from the multiplicative group of its fraction field onto $\mathbf Z$. The trivial valuation on a field is excluded.
refs: Stacks 00PD · equivalent conditions for a discrete valuation ring

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Dedekind domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and every nonzero ideal factors uniquely, up to permutation, into nonzero prime ideals. The unit ideal corresponds to the empty product. Fields are included.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Regular ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and each localization at a prime is a regular local ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Regular local ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and local, and the minimum number of generators of its maximal ideal equals its Krull dimension.

entries.subject: ring-parameters
entries.name: System of parameters
entries.definition: For a Noetherian local ring of dimension $d$, a tuple of $d$ elements of the maximal ideal whose generated ideal has radical equal to the maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 00KU · systems of parameters and regular systems of parameters
entries.ambient: A Noetherian local ring with a specified tuple of length equal to its Krull dimension.

entries.subject: ring-parameters
entries.name: Regular system of parameters
entries.definition: For a Noetherian local ring of dimension $d$, a tuple of $d$ elements generating its maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 00KU · systems of parameters and regular systems of parameters
entries.ambient: A Noetherian local ring with a specified tuple of length equal to its Krull dimension.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Cohen–Macaulay ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and its localization at every prime has depth equal to its Krull dimension.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Cohen–Macaulay local ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and local, and its depth equals its Krull dimension.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Gorenstein ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and each prime localization is Gorenstein as a local ring.
refs: Stacks 0DW7 · global and local Gorenstein rings

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Gorenstein local ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and local, and the complex consisting of the ring in degree zero is a dualizing complex over it.
refs: Stacks 0DW7 · global and local Gorenstein rings

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Complete intersection local ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and local. Its maximal ideal completion is a quotient of a regular local ring by an ideal generated by a regular sequence.
refs: Stacks 09Q3 · local and global complete intersection conditions

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Local complete intersection ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and every prime localization is a complete intersection local ring.
refs: Stacks 09Q3 · local and global complete intersection conditions

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Complete local ring
entries.definition: The ring is local and the canonical map to the inverse limit of the quotients by powers of the maximal ideal is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal
entries.definition: The ring is local and its unique maximal ideal is finitely generated.
refs: Stacks 032B · finite generation and complete local rings

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Cohen ring
entries.definition: The ring is a complete discrete valuation ring with a uniformizer equal to a prime integer.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Henselian local ring
entries.definition: The ring is local and a simple root of the reduction of any monic polynomial lifts to a root over the ring.
refs: Stacks 04GF · henselian and strictly henselian local rings

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Strictly henselian local ring
