entries.definition: The ring is henselian and its residue field is separably closed.
refs: Stacks 04GF · henselian and strictly henselian local rings

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Separably closed residue field
entries.definition: The ring is local and its residue field has no proper finite separable algebraic extension.
refs: Stacks 04GF · residue-field condition for strict henselianity

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Unibranch local ring
entries.definition: The ring is local, its reduction is a domain, and the normalization of that domain in its fraction field is local.
refs: Stacks 0BPZ · unibranch and geometrically unibranch local rings

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Geometrically unibranch local ring
entries.definition: The ring is unibranch, and the residue-field extension of the normalization of its reduction is purely inseparable.
refs: Stacks 0BPZ · unibranch and geometrically unibranch local rings

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Reduction is a domain
entries.definition: The quotient by the nilradical is an integral domain.
refs: Stacks 0BPZ · domain condition in the definition of unibranch

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Serre condition (R₀)
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and its local rings at primes of height zero are regular.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Serre condition (R₁)
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and its local rings at primes of height at most one are regular.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Serre condition (S₁)
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and for every prime localization the depth is at least the smaller of one and its dimension.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Serre condition (S₂)
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and for every prime localization the depth is at least the smaller of two and its dimension.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: No embedded associated primes
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and every associated prime of the ring as a module over itself is a minimal prime.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Condition J-0
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and the regular locus of its prime spectrum contains a nonempty open subset.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Condition J-1
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and the regular locus of its prime spectrum is open.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Condition J-2
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and every finite type algebra over it has open regular locus.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: G-ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and the completion map of each prime localization is regular, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Quasi-excellent ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian, is a G-ring, and satisfies J-2.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Excellent ring
entries.definition: The ring is quasi-excellent and universally catenary.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Nagata ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and for every prime $\mathfrak p$ the normalization of $R/\mathfrak p$ in every finite extension of its fraction field is finite over $R/\mathfrak p$.
refs: Stacks 032R · Nagata rings and Japanese domains

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Universally Japanese ring
entries.definition: For every finite type algebra over the ring that is a domain, the normalization in any finite extension of its fraction field is finite over that domain.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite module
entries.definition: An $R$-module $M$ is finite if some finite family of elements generates it over $R$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finitely presented module
entries.definition: There are nonnegative integers $m,n$ and an exact sequence $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Maps from the module commute with filtered colimits
entries.definition: For every filtered system $(N_i)$ of $R$-modules, the map $\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,\operatorname{colim}_iN_i)$ is bijective.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Free module
entries.definition: There is an $R$-basis of $M$, or equivalently an isomorphism $M\cong R^{(J)}$ for some set $J$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite free module
entries.definition: There is an isomorphism $M\cong R^n$ for a nonnegative integer $n$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Locally free module
entries.definition: Each point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ has a principal open neighbourhood $D(f)$ on which $M_f$ is free, possibly of infinite rank.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite locally free module
entries.definition: Each point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ has a principal open neighbourhood $D(f)$ on which $M_f$ is free of finite rank. The rank can vary with the point.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite locally free module of a prescribed rank
entries.definition: For a fixed nonnegative integer $r$, each point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ has a principal open neighbourhood $D(f)$ on which $M_f\cong R_f^r$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Projective module
entries.definition: The functor $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,-)$ is exact on the category of $R$-modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Injective module
entries.definition: The contravariant functor $\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,M)$ is exact on the category of $R$-modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module with vanishing first Ext out of it
entries.definition: For every $R$-module $N$, $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(M,N)=0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite projective module
entries.definition: The module is both finitely generated and projective.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Direct summand of a free module
entries.definition: There exists an $R$-module $N$ such that $M\oplus N$ is free.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Direct summand of a finite free module
entries.definition: There exists an $R$-module $N$ and a finite $n$ such that $M\oplus N\cong R^n$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Flat module
entries.definition: The functor $M\otimes_R-$ preserves exact sequences of $R$-modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Faithfully flat module
entries.definition: For each complex $N_1\to N_2\to N_3$ of $R$-modules, exactness is equivalent to exactness after tensoring with $M$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Tensor injectivity for finite ideals
entries.definition: For every finitely generated ideal $I\subseteq R$, the multiplication map $I\otimes_R M\to M$ is injective.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Tensor injectivity for all ideals
entries.definition: For every ideal $I\subseteq R$, the multiplication map $I\otimes_R M\to M$ is injective.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Flatness at every maximal ideal
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, $M_\mathfrak m$ is flat over $R_\mathfrak m$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Nonzero fibres at all maximal ideals
entries.definition: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, $M\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak m)\neq0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module with vanishing first Tor against every module
entries.definition: For every $R$-module $N$, $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(M,N)=0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module over a local ring
entries.definition: The base ring has a unique maximal ideal.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module over a Noetherian ring
entries.definition: The base ring satisfies the ascending chain condition on ideals.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module over a domain
entries.definition: The base ring is nonzero and its zero ideal is prime.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module over a valuation ring
entries.definition: The base ring is a domain $R$ such that, for every nonzero $x$ in its fraction field, at least one of $x,x^{-1}$ lies in $R$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Noetherian module
entries.definition: Every ascending chain of submodules stabilizes.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Coherent module
entries.definition: The module is finite and every finite submodule of it is finitely presented.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module with closed support
entries.definition: The set of primes $\mathfrak p$ with $M_\mathfrak p\neq0$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Support of a module
entries.definition: The support of $M$ is the subset $\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R:M_\mathfrak p\ne 0\}$ of the spectrum.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Associated primes of a module
entries.definition: The set $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$ consists of the prime ideals that are annihilators of individual elements of $M$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module with finitely many associated primes
entries.definition: The set $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$ of annihilators of elements that are prime ideals is finite.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Depth with respect to an ideal
entries.definition: For a finite $R$-module $M$ and an ideal $I$, the depth is the supremum of the lengths of $M$-regular sequences in $I$ when $IM\ne M$. It is set to infinity when $IM=M$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Fitting ideals of a module
entries.definition: For a finite $R$-module $M$ with a presentation $R^{(J)}\xrightarrow{A}R^n\to M\to0$, its $k$th Fitting ideal is generated by the minors of size $n-k$ of $A$. These ideals are independent of the presentation. Minors of size zero or less give the unit ideal, and $\operatorname{Fit}_{-1}(M)$ is set to zero.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Localization of a module
entries.definition: For a multiplicative subset $U\subseteq R$, form $U^{-1}M=U^{-1}R\otimes_R M$, with $m/u$ representing the class of the localized element.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Simple module
entries.definition: The module is nonzero and its only submodules are $0$ and $M$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module of finite length
entries.definition: There is a finite filtration from zero to the module with simple successive quotients. The zero module has length zero.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Torsion module over a domain
entries.definition: The base is a domain and each element of the module is annihilated by some nonzero element of the base.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Torsion-free module over a domain
entries.definition: The base is a domain and multiplication by every nonzero scalar is injective on the module.

entries.subject: module-element
entries.name: Torsion element
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, an $R$-module $M$ and $m\in M$, some nonzero $a\in R$ satisfies $am=0$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Mittag-Leffler module
entries.definition: For every directed system of finitely presented $R$-modules with colimit $M$, the associated inverse system obtained by applying $\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,N)$ is Mittag-Leffler for every $R$-module $N$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Sum of countably generated modules
entries.definition: The module is a direct sum of countably generated modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module of finite projective dimension
entries.definition: There is a finite length resolution by projective modules, whose terms need not be finite.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module of finite Tor dimension
entries.definition: $M[0]$ in $D(R)$ has Tor-amplitude in some bounded interval.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module of Tor dimension at most d
entries.definition: For the fixed nonnegative integer $d$, the object $M[0]$ in $D(R)$ has Tor-amplitude in $[-d,0]$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Perfect module
entries.definition: There is a finite length resolution by finite projective modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Pseudo-coherent module
entries.definition: Regarded as $M[0]$ in the derived category, the module is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded above complex of finite free modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module pseudo-coherent in degree m
entries.definition: For the integer $m$ in the statement, there is a bounded complex of finite free modules mapping to $M[0]$ in $D(R)$ and inducing isomorphisms in degrees $>m$ and a surjection in degree $m$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Pseudo-coherent complex
entries.definition: The object of $D(R)$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded above complex of finite free $R$-modules.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Complex pseudo-coherent in degree m
entries.definition: For the integer $m$ in the statement, a bounded complex of finite free modules maps to the given object of $D(R)$, inducing isomorphisms in degrees $>m$ and a surjection in degree $m$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Perfect complex
entries.definition: The object of $D(R)$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective $R$-modules.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Complex with Tor-amplitude in a given interval
entries.definition: For the integers $a\le b$, every $R$-module $M$ satisfies $H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for all $i$ outside $[a,b]$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Complex of finite Tor dimension
entries.definition: There exists a bounded interval containing the Tor-amplitude of the object $K$ in $D(R)$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Cohen–Macaulay module
entries.definition: The base is a Noetherian local ring and the module is finite, with $\operatorname{depth}_R(M)=\dim(\operatorname{Supp}M)$ in the Stacks convention.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Maximal Cohen–Macaulay module
entries.definition: The base is a Noetherian local ring and $M$ is finite with $\operatorname{depth}_R(M)=\dim R$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Finitely generated ideal
entries.definition: The ideal is generated as an ideal by a finite family of elements.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Principal ideal
entries.definition: The ideal is generated by a single element $f$, so it equals $fR$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Radical ideal
entries.definition: The ideal equals its radical $\sqrt I=\{r\in R:r^n\in I\text{ for some }n\ge1\}$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Prime ideal
entries.definition: The quotient $R/I$ is a domain, in particular $I\ne R$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Maximal ideal
entries.definition: The quotient $R/I$ is a field. Equivalently, $I$ is maximal among proper ideals of $R$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Nilpotent ideal
entries.definition: There is an integer $n\ge1$ for which $I^n=0$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Locally nilpotent ideal
entries.definition: For every $x\in I$ there is an integer $n\ge1$ with $x^n=0$. This exponent may depend on $x$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Ideal in a Noetherian ring
entries.definition: The ambient ring satisfies the ascending chain condition on ideals.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Pure ideal
entries.definition: The quotient $R/I$ is flat as an $R$-module.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Ideal generated by an idempotent
entries.definition: There is an element $e\in R$ with $e^2=e$ and $I=eR$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Ideal with local unit for each element
entries.definition: For each $x\in I$ there exists $y\in I$ with $xy=x$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Ideal with a common unit for each finite subset
entries.definition: For every finite family $x_i\in I$ there is one $y\in I$ with $yx_i=x_i$ for all $i$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Ideal satisfying the intersection-product test
entries.definition: For every ideal $J\subseteq R$ one has $I\cap J=IJ$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Ideal with projective quotient
entries.definition: The quotient $R/I$ is a projective $R$-module.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Regular ideal
entries.definition: For every $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$, there is an $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $I_f$ is generated in $R_f$ by a regular sequence.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Koszul-regular ideal
entries.definition: For every $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$, there is an $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $I_f$ has generators in $R_f$ whose Koszul homology vanishes in positive degrees.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: H₁-regular ideal
entries.definition: For every $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$, there is an $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $I_f$ has generators in $R_f$ whose first Koszul homology vanishes.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Quasi-regular ideal
entries.definition: For every $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$, there is an $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $I_f$ has generators $a_1,\dots,a_r$ inducing an isomorphism $(R_f/I_f)[X_1,\dots,X_r]\to\operatorname{gr}_{I_f}(R_f)$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Ideal of definition in a Noetherian local ring
entries.definition: In a Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, an ideal $I$ with $\sqrt I=\mathfrak m$.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Ideal with finite projective conormal module
entries.definition: The quotient $I/I^2$ is a finite projective $R/I$-module.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Radical of an ideal
entries.definition: The radical of $I$ is the ideal $\sqrt I=\{r\in R:r^n\in I\text{ for some }n\ge1\}$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map of finite type
entries.definition: There is a surjection $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ of $R$-algebras for a finite $n$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map of finite presentation
entries.definition: There is a presentation $S\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ with both $m$ and $n$ finite.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Finite ring map
entries.definition: The target $S$ is finite as a module over $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with finitely presented target module
entries.definition: The target $S$ is finitely presented as a module over $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with finite free target module
entries.definition: The target $S$ is free of finite rank as a module over $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Integral ring map
entries.definition: Every element of $S$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $R$.

entries.subject: algebra-element
entries.name: Integral element
entries.definition: For a ring map $R\to S$ and an element $s\in S$, there is a monic $F\in R[T]$ whose image in $S[T]$ vanishes at $s$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Flat ring map
entries.definition: The target $S$ is flat as a module over $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Faithfully flat ring map
entries.definition: The target $S$ is faithfully flat as a module over $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with Noetherian source
entries.definition: The source ring satisfies the ascending chain condition on ideals.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with valuation-ring source
entries.definition: The source is a valuation ring in the sense of Stacks, in particular a domain.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Algebra over a field
entries.definition: The source is a field. The target is an arbitrary algebra over that field.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Algebra over a perfect field
entries.definition: The source is a field whose every algebraic extension is separable.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with reduced target
entries.definition: The target has no nonzero nilpotent elements.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Geometrically reduced algebra over a field
entries.definition: The source is a field $k$ and $K\otimes_k S$ is reduced for every field extension $K/k$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Geometrically irreducible algebra over a field
entries.definition: The source is a field $k$ and for every field extension $K/k$ the spectrum of $K\otimes_k S$ is nonempty and irreducible.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Geometrically connected algebra over a field
entries.definition: The source is a field $k$ and for every field extension $K/k$ the spectrum of $K\otimes_k S$ is connected.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Geometrically normal algebra over a field
entries.definition: The source is a field $k$ and $K\otimes_k S$ is normal for every field extension $K/k$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Geometrically regular Noetherian algebra over a field
entries.definition: The source is a field $k$, the target is Noetherian, and $K\otimes_k S$ is regular for every finitely generated field extension $K/k$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Geometrically integral algebra over a field
entries.definition: The source is a field $k$ and $K\otimes_k S$ is a domain for every field extension $K/k$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Surjective ring map
entries.definition: Every element of the target has a preimage.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Injective ring map
entries.definition: The kernel of the ring map is zero.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Epimorphism of rings
entries.definition: For every ring $T$ and every pair of maps $g,h:S\to T$, equality of the two composites with $R\to S$ implies $g=h$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Tensor multiplication is an isomorphism
entries.definition: The multiplication map $S\otimes_R S\to S$ is an isomorphism of rings.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map injective on spectra
entries.definition: The contraction map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is injective on points.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Going up for prime ideals
entries.definition: For $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak p'$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ over $\mathfrak p$, some $\mathfrak q'\supseteq\mathfrak q$ lies over $\mathfrak p'$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Going down for prime ideals
entries.definition: For $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak p'$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ over $\mathfrak p'$, some $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak q'$ lies over $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Incomparability of distinct primes in each fibre
entries.definition: Distinct primes of $S$ contracting to the same prime of $R$ are incomparable under inclusion.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring isomorphism
entries.definition: The map has a two-sided inverse in the category of rings.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map surjective on spectra
entries.definition: For every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ some $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map universally surjective on spectra
entries.definition: For every base change $R\to R'$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_R S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ is surjective.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Surjective ring map with finitely generated kernel
entries.definition: The map is surjective and its kernel is finitely generated as an ideal of $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Localization map
entries.definition: For some multiplicative subset $U\subseteq R$, the map is isomorphic over $R$ to $R\to U^{-1}R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Principal localization map
entries.definition: For some $f\in R$, the map is isomorphic over $R$ to $R\to R_f$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Localization at an idempotent
entries.definition: For some $e\in R$ with $e^2=e$, the map is isomorphic over $R$ to $R\to R_e$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Maps from the algebra commute with directed colimits
entries.definition: For every directed system $(A_i)$ of $R$-algebras, the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}_R(S,A_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(S,\operatorname{colim}_i A_i)$ is bijective.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Quasi-finite ring map
entries.definition: The map is of finite type and for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ the fibre algebra $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite-dimensional over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with finite-dimensional fibre algebras
entries.definition: For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ has finite dimension as a vector space.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Smooth ring map
entries.definition: The map is of finite presentation, $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{S/R})=0$, and $\Omega_{S/R}$ is finite projective over $S$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Standard smooth ring map
entries.definition: There is a presentation $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ for which a $c$ by $c$ minor of the Jacobian matrix is invertible in $S$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Standard étale ring map
entries.definition: There are polynomials $f,g\in R[x]$ with $f$ monic and an isomorphism $S\cong R[x]_g/(f)$ under which the image of $f'$ is invertible.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Syntomic ring map
entries.definition: The map is flat and of finite presentation, and its fibre algebras over every $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are local complete intersections over the respective fields.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Local complete intersection ring map
entries.definition: The map is of finite type and the kernel of some finite polynomial presentation $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ is a Koszul-regular ideal.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Étale ring map
entries.definition: The map is of finite presentation and the naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}$ is quasi-isomorphic to zero.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Finite étale ring map
entries.definition: The map is both finite and étale.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Unramified ring map
entries.definition: The map is of finite type and $\Omega_{S/R}=0$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: G-unramified ring map
entries.definition: The map is of finite presentation and $\Omega_{S/R}=0$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with vanishing differentials
entries.definition: The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{S/R}$ vanishes.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with vanishing first naive cotangent homology
entries.definition: The first homology $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{S/R})$ of the naive cotangent complex vanishes.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ring map with finite projective differentials
entries.definition: The module $\Omega_{S/R}$ is finite projective over $S$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Formally smooth ring map
entries.definition: For each $R$-algebra $B$, square-zero ideal $J\subseteq B$, and $R$-algebra map $S\to B/J$, an $R$-algebra lift $S\to B$ exists.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Formally unramified ring map
entries.definition: For each $R$-algebra $B$, square-zero ideal $J\subseteq B$, and $R$-algebra map $S\to B/J$, at most one $R$-algebra lift $S\to B$ exists.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Formally étale ring map
entries.definition: For each $R$-algebra $B$, square-zero ideal $J\subseteq B$, and $R$-algebra map $S\to B/J$, exactly one $R$-algebra lift $S\to B$ exists.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Smooth at a target prime
entries.definition: For the chosen $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, there exists $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to S_g$ is smooth.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Étale at a target prime
entries.definition: For the chosen $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, there exists $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to S_g$ is étale.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Standard étale on a principal neighbourhood
entries.definition: For the chosen $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, there exists $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to S_g$ is standard étale.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Unramified at a target prime
entries.definition: For the chosen $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, there exists $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to S_g$ is unramified.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: G-unramified at a target prime
entries.definition: For the chosen $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, there exists $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to S_g$ is G-unramified.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Quasi-finite at a target prime
entries.definition: The map is of finite type and, for $\mathfrak p$ the contraction of $\mathfrak q$, the point of $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ is isolated.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Chosen point of a finite type ring map
entries.definition: The ring map $R\to S$ is of finite type. The chosen target prime is unrestricted.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Finite presentation near a target prime
entries.definition: For the chosen $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, there exists $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to S_g$ is of finite presentation.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Flatness at a target prime
entries.definition: Writing $\mathfrak p$ for the contraction of $\mathfrak q$, the local ring homomorphism $R_\mathfrak p\to S_\mathfrak q$ is flat.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Smooth fibre at a target prime
entries.definition: For $\mathfrak p$ the contraction of $\mathfrak q$, the fibre algebra $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is smooth over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ at the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime
entries.definition: Writing $\mathfrak p$ for the contraction of $\mathfrak q$, one has $\mathfrak pS_\mathfrak q=\mathfrak qS_\mathfrak q$.

entries.subject: ring-map-point
entries.name: Finite separable residue extension at a target prime
entries.definition: The field extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is finite and separable, where $\mathfrak p$ is the contraction of $\mathfrak q$.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Subfield
entries.definition: For an ambient field $E$, a subfield is a unital subring $F\subseteq E$ that is a field.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Characteristic of a field
entries.definition: The characteristic of $F$ is $0$ if $\mathbf Z\to F$ is injective and otherwise is the positive generator of its kernel. A positive characteristic is a prime.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Prime subfield
entries.definition: The smallest subfield of $F$ is the fraction field of the image of $\mathbf Z\to F$. It is canonically $\mathbf Q$ in characteristic $0$, and $\mathbf F_p$ in characteristic $p>0$.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Characteristic zero
entries.definition: The unital map $\mathbf Z\to F$ is injective.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Positive characteristic
entries.definition: There is a prime $p$ for which $p1_F=0$. This prime is unique.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Finite field
entries.definition: The underlying set of the field is finite.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Number field
entries.definition: The field has characteristic $0$ and is finite-dimensional over its prime subfield $\mathbf Q$.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Perfect field
entries.definition: Every field extension of $F$ is separable over $F$ in the general sense of Stacks 030O.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Positive characteristic with surjective Frobenius
entries.definition: The field has characteristic $p>0$, and $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective on the field.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Separably closed field
entries.definition: The field has no proper separable algebraic extension.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Field extension
entries.definition: A field extension $E/F$ consists of fields and a specified inclusion $F\hookrightarrow E$.

entries.subject: field-tower
entries.name: Tower of field extensions
entries.definition: A sequence of field inclusions $F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_n$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Trivial extension
entries.definition: The specified inclusion $F\hookrightarrow E$ is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Base field of characteristic zero
entries.definition: The base field $F$ of $E/F$ has characteristic $0$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Base field of positive characteristic
entries.definition: The base field $F$ of $E/F$ has characteristic $p$ for a prime $p$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite base field
entries.definition: The underlying set of the base field $F$ of $E/F$ is finite.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite target field
entries.definition: The underlying set of the target field $E$ of $E/F$ is finite.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Finite multiplicative subgroups are cyclic
entries.definition: Every finite subgroup of $F^\times$ is cyclic.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: Subfield generated by a family
entries.definition: For a family of elements of $E$ over $F$, form the smallest subfield of $E$ containing $F$ and the image of the family.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finitely generated field extension
entries.definition: There are finitely many elements $a_i\in E$ such that $E=F(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ as a field.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Countably generated field extension
entries.definition: There is a finite or countably infinite set of elements of $E$ that generates it as a field over $F$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Simple field extension
entries.definition: There is an element $a\in E$ such that $E=F(a)$.

entries.subject: field-element
entries.name: Primitive element
entries.definition: For a finite extension $E/F$, an element $a\in E$ is primitive if $E=F(a)$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Degree of an extension
entries.definition: The dimension of $E$ as an $F$-vector space, written $[E:F]$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite field extension
entries.definition: The vector space dimension $[E:F]$ is finite.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finitely many intermediate fields
entries.definition: The set of fields $M$ with $F\subseteq M\subseteq E$ is finite.

entries.subject: field-element
entries.name: Algebraic element
entries.definition: An element $a\in E$ is algebraic over $F$ if some nonzero $P\in F[X]$ vanishes at $a$.

entries.subject: field-element
entries.name: Transcendental element
entries.definition: The element $a\in E$ is a root of no nonzero polynomial in $F[X]$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Algebraic field extension
entries.definition: Every element of $E$ is algebraic over $F$.
refs: Stacks 09GC · algebraicity of an element or extension
Stacks 030J · algebraic extensions in the review

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Every simple subextension is finite
entries.definition: For each $a\in E$, the extension $F(a)/F$ is finite.

entries.subject: field-element
entries.name: Minimal polynomial
entries.definition: For an algebraic element $a$ over $F$, the unique monic generator of the kernel of evaluation $F[X]\to E$, $X\mapsto a$. It is irreducible.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Algebraically closed field
entries.definition: Every algebraic extension of the field is trivial.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Every irreducible polynomial is linear
entries.definition: Every irreducible in $F[X]$ has degree $1$.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Every nonconstant polynomial has a root
entries.definition: Each polynomial of positive degree in $F[X]$ has a root in $F$.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Every nonconstant polynomial splits
entries.definition: Each polynomial of positive degree in $F[X]$ is a scalar multiple of a product of linear factors over $F$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Algebraic closure
entries.definition: The extension $E/F$ is algebraic and $E$ is algebraically closed.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Algebraically closed target field
entries.definition: The target field $E$ of $E/F$ is algebraically closed.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Relative algebraic closure
entries.definition: For $E/F$, take the subfield of $E$ consisting of the elements algebraic over $F$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Base field algebraically closed in the target
entries.definition: Each element of $E$ algebraic over $F$ already lies in $F$.

entries.subject: field-polynomial-pair
entries.name: Relatively prime polynomials
entries.definition: The pair $P,Q\in F[X]$ generates the unit ideal.

entries.subject: field-polynomial-pair
entries.name: No common root in an algebraic closure
entries.definition: There is no element of an algebraic closure of $F$ at which both $P$ and $Q$ vanish.

entries.subject: field-polynomial
entries.name: Irreducible polynomial
entries.definition: The polynomial is a nonzero nonunit in $F[X]$ and every factorization has a unit factor.

entries.subject: field-polynomial
entries.name: Nonzero formal derivative
entries.definition: The formal derivative $P\prime$ in $F[X]$ is nonzero.

entries.subject: field-polynomial
entries.name: Only simple roots in an algebraic closure
entries.definition: The polynomial is nonzero and no root in an algebraic closure has multiplicity greater than one.

entries.subject: field-polynomial
entries.name: Separable irreducible polynomial
entries.definition: The polynomial $P\in F[X]$ is irreducible and is relatively prime to its formal derivative.

entries.subject: field-element
entries.name: Separable algebraic element
entries.definition: The element is algebraic over $F$ and its minimal polynomial is separable.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Separable algebraic extension
entries.definition: The extension $E/F$ is algebraic and every element of $E$ is separable over $F$.
refs: Stacks 030J · algebraic extensions in the review

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Separably generated extension
entries.definition: There is a transcendence basis $S$ of $E/F$ such that $E/F(S)$ is separable algebraic.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Separable field extension
entries.definition: Every subextension finitely generated over the base admits a transcendence basis over the base after adjoining which the remaining extension is separable algebraic.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finitely generated and separably generated extension
entries.definition: The field extension is finitely generated and it admits a transcendence basis such that the extension over the field it generates is separable algebraic.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Geometrically reduced field extension
entries.definition: For every extension $F\subset F\prime$, the ring $E\otimes_F F\prime$ is reduced.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Formally smooth field extension
entries.definition: For any $F$-algebra $A$ with a square-zero ideal $I$, each $F$-algebra map $E\to A/I$ lifts to an $F$-algebra map $E\to A$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Vanishing relative differentials
entries.definition: The $E$-vector space of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{E/F}$ is zero.

entries.subject: field-polynomial
entries.name: Separable degree of an irreducible polynomial
entries.definition: The number of distinct roots of an irreducible $P\in F[X]$ in an algebraic closure of $F$.

entries.subject: field-element
entries.name: Purely inseparable element
entries.definition: In characteristic $p>0$, some power $a^{p^r}$ lies in $F$, where $r\geq0$. In characteristic zero the convention here is $a\in F$, so that $F(a)/F$ is purely inseparable exactly when the element is.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Purely inseparable extension
entries.definition: Either $E=F$, or $F$ has characteristic $p>0$ and each $a\in E$ has $a^{p^r}\in F$ for some $r\geq0$ depending on $a$.
refs: Stacks 030J · the review formulates the positive-characteristic case

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Purely inseparable extension in positive characteristic
entries.definition: The base has characteristic $p>0$ and every $a\in E$ has $a^{p^r}\in F$ for some $r\geq0$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Maximal separable subextension
entries.definition: For an algebraic extension $E/F$, the elements separable over $F$ form the unique intermediate field $E_s$ for which $E_s/F$ is separable and $E/E_s$ is purely inseparable.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Separable degree of an extension
entries.definition: For an algebraic extension $E/F$, the degree $[E_s:F]$ of its maximal separable subextension.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Inseparable degree of an extension
entries.definition: For an algebraic extension $E/F$, the degree $[E:E_s]$ over its maximal separable subextension.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite extension with the maximal number of embeddings
entries.definition: The extension is finite, and the number of $F$-embeddings of $E$ into an algebraic closure of $F$ is $[E:F]$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Normal field extension
entries.definition: The extension $E/F$ is algebraic and the minimal polynomial over $F$ of each $a\in E$ splits over $E$, with multiplicities allowed.
refs: Stacks 030J · algebraic extensions in the review

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Algebraic extension with a common image for all embeddings
entries.definition: The extension is algebraic, and all $F$-embeddings into a chosen algebraic closure of $F$ have the same image.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite extension with as many automorphisms as its separable degree
entries.definition: The extension is finite, and $|\operatorname{Aut}_F(E)|=[E:F]_s$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Group of automorphisms over the base
entries.definition: The group $\operatorname{Aut}_F(E)$ of field automorphisms of $E$ that fix every element of $F$.

entries.subject: field-map
entries.name: Automorphism of a field extension
entries.definition: For a field extension $E/F$, an automorphism is a bijective $F$-homomorphism $E\to E$.

entries.subject: field-polynomial
entries.name: Splitting field of a polynomial
entries.definition: For a nonconstant polynomial $P\in F[X]$, this is the subfield generated over $F$ by all its roots in a chosen algebraic closure.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Normal closure of a finite extension
entries.definition: After embedding a finite $E/F$ in an algebraic closure, take the smallest subfield containing $E$ that is normal over $F$. It is finite over $F$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Galois extension
entries.definition: The extension $E/F$ is algebraic, separable and normal.
refs: Stacks 030J · algebraic extensions in the review

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Galois group
entries.definition: For a Galois extension $E/F$, the group of $F$-automorphisms of $E$ is denoted $\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Krull topology on the Galois group
entries.definition: For a Galois extension, give $E$ the discrete topology and give the Galois group the topology of pointwise convergence on $E$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite extension with as many automorphisms as its degree
entries.definition: The extension is finite, and $|\operatorname{Aut}_F(E)|=[E:F]$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite cyclic Galois extension
entries.definition: The extension is finite Galois, with cyclic Galois group.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Field trace
entries.definition: For a finite extension $E/F$, the field trace of $a\in E$ is the trace of multiplication by $a$ on the $F$-vector space $E$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Field norm
entries.definition: For a finite extension $E/F$, the field norm of $a\in E$ is the determinant of multiplication by $a$ on the $F$-vector space $E$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Trace pairing
entries.definition: For a finite extension $E/F$, take the symmetric $F$-bilinear form $(a,b)\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(ab)$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Discriminant of a finite field extension
entries.definition: Take the discriminant of the trace pairing of a finite field extension, using its determinant modulo squares of nonzero base-field scalars when the determinant is nonzero.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite extension with nonzero trace map
entries.definition: The extension is finite and its $F$-linear trace map $E\to F$ is not the zero map.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite extension with nondegenerate trace pairing
entries.definition: The extension is finite and its trace pairing has zero radical.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Finite extension with nonzero discriminant
entries.definition: The extension is finite, and the determinant of the matrix of its trace pairing in any basis is nonzero.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: Algebraically independent family
entries.definition: For a family $(a_i)_{i\in I}$ in $E$, the $F$-algebra map $F[X_i:i\in I]\to E$ sending $X_i$ to $a_i$ is injective.

entries.subject: field
entries.name: Rational function field
entries.definition: For a field $F$ and a set $I$, take the fraction field of the polynomial algebra $F[X_i:i\in I]$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Purely transcendental extension
entries.definition: There is an $F$-isomorphism from a rational function field in some set of indeterminates over $F$ to $E$. The set may be empty.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: Target algebraic over the field generated by the family
entries.definition: For $(a_i)_{i\in I}$ in $E$, the field $E$ is algebraic over $F(a_i:i\in I)$.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: Transcendence basis
entries.definition: The family is algebraically independent over $F$ and $E$ is algebraic over the subfield generated by the family over $F$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Transcendence degree
entries.definition: The cardinality of a transcendence basis of $E$ over $F$.

entries.subject: field-extension
entries.name: Transcendence degree zero
entries.definition: A transcendence basis of $E/F$ has zero cardinality.

entries.subject: field-extension-pair
entries.name: Compositum in a common overfield
entries.definition: For subfields $E,L\subseteq\Omega$ containing $F$, the compositum $EL$ is the smallest subfield of $\Omega$ containing both $E$ and $L$.

entries.subject: field-extension-pair
entries.name: Linearly disjoint subfields
entries.definition: For subfields $E,L\subseteq\Omega$ containing $F$, the multiplication map $E\otimes_F L\to EL$ is injective.

entries.subject: field-extension-pair
entries.name: Linear independence preserved in the compositum
entries.definition: For subfields $E,L\subseteq\Omega$ containing $F$, every $F$-linearly independent finite tuple in $E$ remains $L$-linearly independent in $EL$.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Ideal in the Jacobson radical
entries.definition: The pair $(A,I)$ satisfies $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)=\bigcap_{\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Max}A}\mathfrak m$.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Lifting comaximal monic factorizations
entries.definition: For each monic $f\in A[T]$ and each factorization of its image in $(A/I)[T]$ into two comaximal monic factors, there is a monic factorization in $A[T]$ reducing to the chosen one.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Henselian pair
entries.definition: The ideal $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $A$, and comaximal monic factorizations lift along $A\to A/I$.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Locally nilpotent ideal in a pair
entries.definition: Every element of $I$ has some positive power equal to zero in $A$. In a commutative ring this is equivalent to nilpotence of every finitely generated subideal of $I$.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Adically complete pair
entries.definition: The canonical map $A\to\varprojlim_n A/I^n$ is an isomorphism. This includes separatedness for the $I$-adic topology.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Idempotent bijection for the pair
entries.definition: Reduction induces a bijection between idempotents of $A$ and of $A/I$.
refs: Stacks 09XI · specialization of the finite-algebra criterion to B = A

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Idempotent bijection in all finite algebras
entries.definition: For every finite $A$-algebra $B$, reduction induces a bijection on idempotents from $B$ to $B/IB$.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Idempotent bijection in all integral algebras
entries.definition: For every integral $A$-algebra $B$, reduction induces a bijection on idempotents from $B$ to $B/IB$.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Lifting sections of étale algebras
entries.definition: For each étale $A$-algebra $B$, every $A$-algebra map $B\to A/I$ lifts to an $A$-algebra map $B\to A$.

entries.subject: ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Roots in the residue class of one
entries.definition: For all $n\geq 1$ and $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in I$, the polynomial $T^n(T-1)+\sum_{i=0}^n a_iT^i$ has a root in $1+I$.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Residue field of a local ring
entries.definition: For a local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ the residue field is the quotient $R/\mathfrak m$. The quotient map is defined using the unique maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 07BI · residue field of a local ring

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Local homomorphism of local rings
entries.definition: A unital map $R\to S$ of local rings is local if it sends the maximal ideal of $R$ into the maximal ideal of $S$. Equivalently the preimage of the maximal ideal of $S$ is the maximal ideal of $R$.
refs: Stacks 07BI · local homomorphism of local rings

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Regular ring map
entries.definition: A map $R\to A$ is regular if it is flat and each fibre $A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Map between Noetherian rings
entries.definition: Both the source ring and the target ring are Noetherian.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Filtered colimit of smooth algebras
entries.definition: For a map $R\to A$, the $R$-algebra $A$ is isomorphic to a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.
refs: Stacks 07EP · regularity of smooth colimits with Noetherian fibres

theorems.subject: qcqs-cover
theorems.proof: After base change to $\operatorname{Spec}V$, a faithfully flat cover lifts the specialization from the generic point to the closed point. A valuation-ring extension dominating that lifted specialization gives the required square. For general families use an affine-local standard fpqc refinement.
refs: Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph
theorems.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
theorems.name: Fpqc topology is coarser than Valuative (v) topology

theorems.subject: qcqs-cover
theorems.proof: Given a proper surjection, choose a point over the generic point after base change to $\operatorname{Spec}V$. Extend the valuation to the residue field of the chosen point and use the valuative criterion of properness. Zariski covers already satisfy the valuation test.
refs: Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph
theorems.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
theorems.name: Ph topology is coarser than Valuative (v) topology

theorems.subject: qcqs-cover
theorems.proof: The valuation test can be expressed as lifting the specialization from the generic point to the closed point after base change to a valuation spectrum. Over a rank-one valuation ring, lifting that pair of points yields an extension of rank one. Thus an arbitrary-rank cover satisfies the rank-at-most-one test. See Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 2.5 of Bhatt–Mathew.
refs: Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of étale morphisms
theorems.ambient: The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.
theorems.name: Valuative (v) topology is coarser than Arc topology

theorems.subject: ring

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The presentation includes a surjection from a finite free module.
theorems.name: Finitely presented module ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A lift against a surjective map can be chosen on each basis vector.
theorems.name: Free module ⇒ Projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensoring with a free module gives a direct sum of copies of the input. Direct sums preserve exact sequences.
theorems.name: Free module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: If the base ring is nonzero, an infinite free basis cannot be generated by finitely many vectors with finite support. Over the zero ring the module is zero and admits the empty basis.
theorems.name: Finite module + Free module ⇔ Finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A surjection from a free module onto a projective module splits, and a summand of a projective module is projective.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇔ Direct summand of a free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The first Ext group vanishes for projective modules, and its vanishing against every module splits any short exact sequence ending in the module.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇔ Module with vanishing first Ext out of it

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Projectivity implies flatness by the characterization. Equivalently, a direct summand of a flat module is flat.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: This is the finite-generation and projectivity condition together.
theorems.name: Finite module + Projective module ⇔ Finite projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The finite-projective-module theorem identifies these two conditions.
theorems.name: Finitely presented module + Flat module ⇔ Finite projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Projectivity splits a finite free surjection, and a summand of a finite free module is finite projective.
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇔ Direct summand of a finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective module is finite locally free. Conversely, finite local freeness gives finite presentation and flatness.
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇔ Finite locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use the same principal open covering and forget the fixed value of the rank.
theorems.name: Finite locally free module of a prescribed rank ⇒ Finite locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use the same principal open covering and forget the finiteness of the rank.
theorems.name: Finite locally free module ⇒ Locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Each localization at a maximal ideal is free, hence flat.
theorems.name: Locally free module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Lift a basis of the residue fibre. Nakayama gives a surjection, and flatness makes the lifted family a basis.
theorems.name: Module over a local ring + Finite module + Flat module ⇒ Finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Kaplansky’s theorem applies without finite-generation assumptions.
theorems.name: Module over a local ring + Projective module ⇒ Free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The kernel of a finite free presentation is a submodule of a finite module over a Noetherian ring, hence finite.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring + Finite module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Every submodule is finite. This is equivalent to the ascending chain condition.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring + Finite module ⇒ Noetherian module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A module with the ascending chain condition has a maximal finitely generated submodule, which must be the whole module.
theorems.name: Noetherian module ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The module is a finite submodule of itself.
theorems.name: Coherent module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Every finite submodule is finitely presented over a Noetherian base.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring + Finite module ⇒ Coherent module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The finite-ideal criterion for flatness is valid over any ring.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Tensor injectivity for finite ideals

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The ideal criterion for flatness is valid over any ring.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Tensor injectivity for all ideals

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Flatness gives vanishing of the derived functors of tensor. Conversely, the Tor exact sequence gives the injectivity of tensoring any inclusion.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Module with vanishing first Tor against every module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensor kernels are detected after localizing at maximal ideals.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Flatness at every maximal ideal

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The fibre criterion for a flat module detects faithful flatness.
theorems.name: Flat module + Nonzero fibres at all maximal ideals ⇔ Faithfully flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The support of a finite module is the vanishing set of its annihilator.
theorems.name: Finite module ⇒ Module with closed support

theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring + Finite module ⇒ Module with finitely many associated primes

theorems.name: Module of finite length ⇒ Finite module

theorems.proof: Strict inclusions increase length, which is bounded by the length of the module.

theorems.proof: The characterization of projectivity yields both conditions.

theorems.proof: A finite projective resolution computes derived tensor and is bounded.

theorems.proof: Localization is an exact tensor functor.

theorems.subject: ring-map

theorems.subject: ring-map

theorems.subject: ring-map

theorems.subject: ring-map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The standard smooth presentation locally on the target is syntomic.
theorems.name: Smooth ring map ⇒ Syntomic ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A Koszul-regular ideal is quasi-regular, hence finitely generated. Thus a finite polynomial presentation of a local complete intersection map is finitely presented.
theorems.name: Local complete intersection ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The flat local-complete-intersection criterion is equivalent to the fibre definition.
theorems.name: Flat ring map + Local complete intersection ring map ⇔ Syntomic ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finite presentation occurs in the definition of a syntomic map.
theorems.name: Syntomic ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The naive cotangent complex is quasi-isomorphic to zero precisely when both its homology modules vanish.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation + Ring map with vanishing first naive cotangent homology + Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The zero module is finite projective. An étale map meets the smoothness criterion with zero differentials.
theorems.name: Étale ring map ⇒ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The criterion requires both flatness and G-unramifiedness, hence finite presentation.
theorems.name: Flat ring map + G-unramified ring map ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Étale maps are quasi-finite.
theorems.name: Étale ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The condition is the conjunction of finiteness and étaleness.
theorems.name: Finite ring map + Étale ring map ⇔ Finite étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: These are the two conditions defining unramifiedness.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite type + Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: G-unramifiedness uses finite presentation together with vanishing relative differentials.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation + Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ G-unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: For a square-zero extension, the difference of two lifts is a derivation and conversely one may add any derivation to a lift.
theorems.name: Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Formally unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The finite presentation hypothesis is part of the equivalence between smoothness and formal smoothness.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation + Formally smooth ring map ⇔ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Existence and uniqueness of square-zero lifts are exactly the two lifting conditions together.
theorems.name: Formally smooth ring map + Formally unramified ring map ⇔ Formally étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The formal lifting criterion for étaleness requires finite presentation.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation + Formally étale ring map ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: On a principal neighbourhood where the map is étale, it is smooth.
theorems.name: Étale at a target prime ⇒ Smooth at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: An étale presentation on the neighbourhood is G-unramified.
theorems.name: Étale at a target prime ⇒ G-unramified at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: Every étale map near the chosen point is standard étale after further principal localization. The converse follows from standard étale implying étale.
theorems.name: Étale at a target prime ⇔ Standard étale on a principal neighbourhood

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: Intersect the two principal neighbourhoods. Vanishing of differentials localizes, and localizing a finitely presented algebra at one element preserves finite presentation.
theorems.name: Unramified at a target prime + Finite presentation near a target prime ⇔ G-unramified at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: Unramifiedness at the chosen prime gives both residue conditions.
theorems.name: Unramified at a target prime ⇒ Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime + Finite separable residue extension at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: The smooth neighbourhood is flat of finite presentation, and flatness passes to the induced map on local rings.
theorems.name: Smooth at a target prime ⇒ Flatness at a target prime + Finite presentation near a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: These hypotheses give smoothness by the fibre criterion. Conversely, a smooth neighbourhood is flat and finitely presented, and its base change to the residue field is smooth.
theorems.name: Finite presentation near a target prime + Flatness at a target prime + Smooth fibre at a target prime ⇔ Smooth at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: First restrict to the finitely presented principal neighbourhood, then use the flatness and residue conditions there. Conversely, an étale neighbourhood supplies finite presentation, flatness, and the stated residue conditions.
theorems.name: Finite presentation near a target prime + Flatness at a target prime + Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime + Finite separable residue extension at a target prime ⇔ Étale at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: The finite-type hypothesis allows the quasi-finiteness criterion for the fibre at the chosen prime.
theorems.name: Unramified at a target prime + Chosen point of a finite type ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: For a finite-type map, the condition on the maximal ideal and separability of the residue extension give unramifiedness at the chosen point.
theorems.name: Chosen point of a finite type ring map + Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime + Finite separable residue extension at a target prime ⇒ Unramified at a target prime

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.proof: A finite Tor-amplitude bound lets one truncate the pseudo-coherent resolution to a bounded complex of finite projective modules.
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent complex + Complex of finite Tor dimension ⇔ Perfect complex

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.proof: The specified interval provides the required bound.
theorems.name: Complex with Tor-amplitude in a given interval ⇒ Complex of finite Tor dimension

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: A characteristic-zero field contains the infinite prime subfield $\mathbf Q$.
theorems.name: Finite field ⇒ Positive characteristic

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: A number field is a finite extension of $\mathbf Q$, so its characteristic is zero.
theorems.name: Number field ⇒ Characteristic zero

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: The characteristic-zero case of the criterion for a perfect field.
theorems.name: Characteristic zero ⇒ Perfect field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: The positive-characteristic case of the criterion for a perfect field.
theorems.name: Positive characteristic with surjective Frobenius ⇒ Perfect field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: A finite field has positive characteristic. Frobenius is injective on a field and thus surjective on the finite underlying set.
theorems.name: Finite field ⇒ Positive characteristic with surjective Frobenius

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Every separable algebraic extension is algebraic and hence trivial.
theorems.name: Algebraically closed field ⇒ Separably closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: In positive characteristic, a root of $X^p-a$ lies in an algebraically closed field, for every element $a$. In characteristic zero every field is perfect.
refs: Stacks 09GR · polynomial criterion for algebraic closedness
theorems.name: Algebraically closed field ⇒ Perfect field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Over a perfect field, every algebraic extension is separable. If the field is also separably closed, each algebraic extension is therefore trivial. An algebraically closed field is perfect and separably closed.
theorems.name: Perfect field + Separably closed field ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Apply the minimal polynomial criterion to algebraic elements.
theorems.name: Every irreducible polynomial is linear ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: An irreducible polynomial with a root is linear, and algebraic closedness ensures every nonconstant polynomial has a root.
theorems.name: Every nonconstant polynomial has a root ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Factor a polynomial into irreducibles. Splitting implies that every irreducible is linear.
theorems.name: Every nonconstant polynomial splits ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field-polynomial-pair
theorems.proof: A nonconstant common irreducible factor gives a common root in an algebraic closure. A Bézout identity precludes a common root.
theorems.name: No common root in an algebraic closure ⇔ Relatively prime polynomials

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.proof: For an irreducible polynomial the derivative is relatively prime to the polynomial whenever it is nonzero, since it has smaller degree.
refs: Stacks 09H1 · definition of separable irreducible polynomial
theorems.name: Irreducible polynomial + Nonzero formal derivative ⇔ Separable irreducible polynomial

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.proof: A repeated root in an algebraic closure is precisely a common root of the polynomial and its derivative.
theorems.name: Irreducible polynomial + Only simple roots in an algebraic closure ⇔ Separable irreducible polynomial

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.proof: The separability condition is imposed on the minimal polynomial of an algebraic element.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic element ⇒ Algebraic element

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.proof: In characteristic $p>0$, $a$ is a root of $X^{p^r}-a^{p^r}\in F[X]$. An element of the base field is algebraic in any characteristic.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable element ⇒ Algebraic element

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A single generator gives a finite generating set.
theorems.name: Simple field extension ⇒ Finitely generated field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Every finite set is at most countable.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension ⇒ Countably generated field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Adjoin a finite algebraic generating set successively and multiply its finite degrees. Conversely a finite extension is algebraic, and a finite vector space basis generates the field.
theorems.name: Algebraic field extension + Finitely generated field extension ⇔ Finite field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For an element $a$, the simple extension $F(a)$ is finite exactly when $a$ is algebraic over $F$.
theorems.name: Every simple subextension is finite ⇔ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: These are precisely the two defining conditions on $E/F$.
theorems.name: Algebraic field extension + Algebraically closed target field ⇔ Algebraic closure

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The adjective is used for an algebraic extension whose elements are separable.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Apply the polynomial $X^{p^r}-a^{p^r}$ to each element in positive characteristic, with equality handled in any characteristic.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable extension ⇒ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Once the base has positive characteristic, the general and review definitions of pure inseparability agree.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable extension + Base field of positive characteristic ⇔ Purely inseparable extension in positive characteristic

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For $a^{p^r}\in F$, the polynomial $X^{p^r}-a^{p^r}=(X-a)^{p^r}$ over $E$ is divisible by the minimal polynomial of $a$, which therefore splits over $E$.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable extension ⇒ Normal field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Each minimal polynomial of an element of a separable purely inseparable extension has only one distinct root and is separable, hence has degree one. A trivial extension satisfies both conditions.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic extension + Purely inseparable extension ⇔ Trivial extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: All elements of an algebraic extension lie in its relative algebraic closure; if this is the base field the extension is trivial.
theorems.name: Algebraic field extension + Base field algebraically closed in the target ⇔ Trivial extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The empty set is a transcendence basis of an algebraic extension.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A separably generated extension is separable in the general sense of Stacks 030O.
theorems.name: Separably generated extension ⇒ Separable field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Take the independent generators as transcendence basis. The resulting algebraic extension is trivial and hence separable.
theorems.name: Purely transcendental extension ⇒ Separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a simple subextension generated by an algebraic element, a transcendence basis is empty, so the general criterion forces this element to be separable.
theorems.name: Separable field extension + Algebraic field extension ⇔ Separable algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a finitely generated separable extension, apply the definition of general separability to the whole extension.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension + Separable field extension ⇔ Finitely generated and separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The named condition is a conjunction of the two separately defined predicates.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension + Separably generated extension ⇔ Finitely generated and separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Geometric reducedness characterizes separability of a field extension in either characteristic.
theorems.name: Geometrically reduced field extension ⇔ Separable field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness is equivalent to the general notion of separability for field extensions.
theorems.name: Formally smooth field extension ⇔ Separable field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Each separable minimal polynomial has invertible derivative at its root, forcing the differential of that root to vanish.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Vanishing relative differentials

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The finite-generation hypothesis is part of the criterion.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension + Vanishing relative differentials ⇒ Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A nonconstant polynomial in characteristic zero has nonzero derivative. Apply the criterion to the minimal polynomial of each element.
theorems.name: Base field of characteristic zero + Algebraic field extension ⇒ Separable algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a finite extension the number of embeddings into an algebraic closure is at most the degree, with equality precisely in the separable case.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇔ Finite extension with the maximal number of embeddings

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The primitive element theorem applies to finite separable extensions.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Simple field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Each intermediate field is generated over the base by the coefficients of the minimal polynomial of the primitive element over that intermediate field. This polynomial must be one of the finitely many monic factors over the target.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Simple field extension ⇒ Finitely many intermediate fields

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Over an infinite base, finitely many proper intermediate fields cannot cover the target vector space. For a finite base the target is a finite field with cyclic multiplicative group.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Finitely many intermediate fields ⇒ Simple field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The Stacks definition of normal extension starts with an algebraic extension.
theorems.name: Normal field extension ⇒ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The image under an embedding contains every conjugate of every one of its elements precisely in the normal case.
theorems.name: Algebraic extension with a common image for all embeddings ⇔ Normal field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The automorphism group embeds into the set of embeddings into an algebraic closure, and normality means every such embedding has image the target field.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Normal field extension ⇔ Finite extension with as many automorphisms as its separable degree

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Both properties require algebraicity, and together they are the definition of a Galois extension.
theorems.name: Normal field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇔ Galois extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The number of automorphisms is bounded by the separable degree, which in turn is bounded by the degree. Both equalities hold exactly for a finite Galois extension.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Galois extension ⇔ Finite extension with as many automorphisms as its degree

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The cyclicity condition is imposed on a finite Galois extension.
theorems.name: Finite cyclic Galois extension ⇒ Finite field extension + Galois extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a separable extension the sum of its distinct embeddings is nonzero by independence of characters. In a finite inseparable extension the trace is zero.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇔ Finite extension with nonzero trace map

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: If the trace map is nonzero, choose $c$ of nonzero trace. Each nonzero $a$ pairs nontrivially with $a^{-1}c$. A zero trace map gives the zero pairing on the nonzero vector space.
theorems.name: Finite extension with nonzero trace map ⇔ Finite extension with nondegenerate trace pairing

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The matrix in a basis represents the linear map from the vector space to its dual. It is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero.
theorems.name: Finite extension with nondegenerate trace pairing ⇔ Finite extension with nonzero discriminant

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.proof: These are the two defining conditions on the family.
theorems.name: Algebraically independent family + Target algebraic over the field generated by the family ⇔ Transcendence basis

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The empty family is algebraically independent and generates the base field. It is a transcendence basis precisely if the target is algebraic.
theorems.name: Transcendence degree zero ⇔ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A subfield of a finite field is finite, and a generator of the cyclic group of units of the target generates the extension.
theorems.name: Finite target field ⇒ Finite base field + Finite field extension + Simple field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
