theorems.proof: Write $q=|F|$ and $[E:F]=n$. Every element of $E$ is a root of $X^{q^n}-X$, so $E$ is its splitting field, and the derivative is $-1$. The $q$-power Frobenius fixes $F$ and has order $n$: if its $i$th power were the identity for $0<i<n$, the degree-$q^i$ polynomial $X^{q^i}-X$ would have $q^n$ roots. The Galois group has order $n$, so this element generates it.
theorems.name: Finite target field ⇒ Finite cyclic Galois extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A finite-dimensional vector space over a finite field has finitely many elements.
theorems.name: Finite base field + Finite field extension ⇒ Finite target field

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The rational function field on an empty set of indeterminates is the base field.
theorems.name: Trivial extension ⇒ Purely transcendental extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A rational function involves only finitely many independent variables. In one variable any nonconstant rational function makes that variable algebraic over the subfield it generates. Induct on the number of variables by treating the last one over the rational function field on the others.
theorems.name: Purely transcendental extension ⇒ Base field algebraically closed in the target

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
theorems.proof: Every tensor has a representation using an $F$-linearly independent tuple on the $E$ side. Such tensors map to nonzero elements when any coefficient on the $L$ side is nonzero, precisely by preservation of independence.
theorems.name: Linear independence preserved in the compositum ⇔ Linearly disjoint subfields

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The two defining conditions of a henselian pair
theorems.proof: Both conditions are part of the definition. Neither individual condition is used by itself in this equivalence.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A locally nilpotent ideal gives a henselian pair
theorems.proof: Locally nilpotent thickenings have equivalent étale algebra categories and satisfy the henselian lifting criterion.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: An adically complete pair is henselian
theorems.proof: Successive nilpotent quotients lift comaximal factorizations compatibly. Pass to the inverse limit using completeness.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Finite-algebra idempotent criterion
theorems.proof: The finite-algebra idempotent criterion in the numbered result is equivalent to the defining lifting property.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Integral-algebra idempotent criterion
theorems.proof: The numbered result allows arbitrary integral algebras. Every finite algebra is integral.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Étale section criterion
theorems.proof: This criterion uses all étale algebras over the specified base, with section lifting along the specified quotient.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Gabber root criterion
theorems.proof: The root condition is coupled with the Jacobson radical hypothesis. Under those hypotheses the root in the residue class of one is unique.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The finite-algebra criterion tests the base pair
theorems.proof: Use the finite A-algebra A itself.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: A flat local homomorphism of local rings is faithfully flat
theorems.proof: The maximal ideal of the target lies over the unique maximal ideal of the source. This supplies the nonempty fibre required by the faithful flatness criterion for a flat map.
refs: Stacks 00HR · flat local maps are faithfully flat

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Popescu’s theorem with its Noetherian hypotheses
theorems.hypotheses: Both source and target are Noetherian. The filtered diagram is taken in algebras over the fixed source ring.
theorems.proof: Popescu gives a filtered smooth presentation of the target of a regular homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Conversely the target is flat as a filtered colimit of flat modules, and the fibre rings are Noetherian because each is a localization of a quotient of the target. The smooth colimit criterion applies to those fibres.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The finite qc basis presents Zariski sheaves
theorems.proof: Every open is a union of affine opens. Finite intersections of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact on a quasi-separated scheme, and every open covering of a basis object has a finite basis refinement. Restriction and the usual compatible-section extension therefore give inverse equivalences of sheaf categories.
refs: Stacks 0069 · quasi-compact opens and finite refinements

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Two uses of qc in site terminology
theorems.proof: The finite open basis site uses inclusions of open subsets of a fixed scheme. The Stacks qc topology in Cohomology on Sites §21.31 uses continuous maps between locally quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces. Its comparison theorem uses the latter hypotheses, so it does not automatically apply to the Zariski space of a qcqs scheme.
refs: Stacks 09WY · cohomology on locally quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces
Stacks 0069 · quasi-compact opens and finite refinements

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Recovering the Zariski closed subsets
theorems.proof: For a spectral space, a subset is closed in the original topology exactly when it is closed in the patch topology and stable under specialization. Patch topology alone need not remember the specialization order.
refs: Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The profinite site and condensed sets
theorems.proof: Finite jointly surjective families are closed under pullback and composition, and include the empty family covering the empty space. With a fixed strong limit size bound, the sheaf condition on this site gives the corresponding condensed sets. This compares sites of spaces and is not a refinement relation on schemes.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Comparison with a basis
theorems.proof: For a qcqs scheme the quasi-compact opens form a basis closed under finite intersections. The basis comparison lemma identifies sheaves on all opens with sheaves for the induced basis topology; each cover of a quasi-compact open admits a finite subcover.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Giraud’s characterization
theorems.proof: A Grothendieck topos is characterized, in a fixed universe, by the Giraud axioms: a small generating family, universal small colimits, disjoint coproducts and effective equivalence relations (with the usual categorical hypotheses). A site gives a presentation, not a unique presentation.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Topological invariance of the small étale site
theorems.proof: Pullback along a universal homeomorphism of schemes is an equivalence of small étale sites and yields an equivalence of étale topoi. This statement does not identify the structure sheaves as rings under arbitrary such maps.
refs: Stacks 04DY · topological invariance of the small étale site

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Hochster representation
theorems.proof: Every spectral space is homeomorphic to the prime spectrum of a commutative ring, and every prime spectrum is spectral. The assertion concerns the underlying topological space, without specifying a canonical ring or recovering a scheme structure.
refs: Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings (1969)
Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology
Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, Theorem 6
theorems.hypotheses: Work in classical set theory. Consider a topological space $X$ and commutative rings with identity, allowing the zero ring.
theorems.statement: $X$ is spectral if and only if it is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ for some commutative ring $A$. The equivalence concerns existence of a realization as a topological space.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Coherent locale and spectral space duality
theorems.proof: Classically, bounded distributive lattices are dual to spectral spaces with spectral maps. Prime ideals give the points, and the lattice is recovered as the quasi-compact opens. Ideal completion gives the corresponding coherent frame; the spatial interpretation uses classical prime ideal separation.
refs: Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings (1969)
The patch topology in univalent foundations
Blechschmidt, Generalized spaces for constructive algebra
Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, Theorem 6
Stacks 08YG · definition of a spectral space
theorems.hypotheses: Use classical prime ideal separation, spectral spaces with spectral maps, and coherent locales with maps whose inverse image preserves compact opens.
theorems.statement: Taking the locale of opens and taking the space of points are inverse equivalences. The compact elements of the frame are the quasi-compact opens of the spectral space.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Duality and the invariant patch topology
theorems.proof: In the dual topology the quasi-compact opens are the complements of the original quasi-compact opens. Taking complements twice proves involutivity and adjoining both families gives the same patch topology.
refs: Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings (1969)
Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Little and big Zariski comparison
theorems.proof: For the big site chosen in the thesis, §16 constructs the comparison with the little topos and describes how the structure sheaves and internal statements transform. The restricted affine finite presentation model has its own specified hypotheses and is not being identified here with the entire category of schemes over an arbitrary base.
refs: Blechschmidt, Using the internal language of toposes in algebraic geometry, Parts II–III
Blechschmidt, Using the internal language of toposes, §16
Stacks 020Z · small and big Zariski comparison
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme. Choose a big Zariski site as in Blechschmidt §15, containing the opens of $S$, and let $\operatorname{Sh}(S)$ denote the little Zariski topos.
theorems.statement: The geometric morphism $\pi:\operatorname{Zar}(S)\to\operatorname{Sh}(S)$ is connected and local. The direct image $\pi_*$ is restriction and has a fully faithful right adjoint, giving a section of $\pi$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Restricted functoriality of stack sites
theorems.proof: Smooth maps of algebraic stacks give functoriality for the lisse-étale site; flat maps give it for the flat-fppf site in the cited result. Cohomology of restrictions from the big site is compared separately.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Prismatic–crystalline comparison
theorems.proof: For a bounded crystalline prism with I=(p) and X smooth over A/I in the p-adic formal setting, the Frobenius base change of relative prismatic cohomology is canonically crystalline cohomology: $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{crys}}(X/A)\simeq R\Gamma_{\Delta}(X/A)\widehat{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{A,\varphi_A}A$. This is a cohomology comparison, not a site equivalence.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorems 1.8(1) and 5.2
Stacks 07IG · definition of the small crystalline site
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a bounded prism $(A,I)$ and a smooth $p$-adic formal scheme $X$ over $\operatorname{Spf}(A/I)$. Assume $I=(p)$ and use the canonical divided powers on $(p)$ in the crystalline comparison over the formal base.
theorems.statement: The comparison is a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism of commutative algebras in $D(A)$: $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{crys}}(X/A)\simeq R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)\widehat\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,\varphi_A} A$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Prismatic Hodge–Tate comparison
theorems.proof: For a smooth affine p-adic formal X=Spf R over A/I with (A,I) bounded, the degree i cohomology of the derived reduction of prismatic cohomology modulo I is identified with completed relative i-forms with Breuil–Kisin twist −i. See the affine Hodge–Tate comparison in Theorem 1.8 and §4.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorems 1.8(2) and 6.3
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a bounded prism $(A,I)$ and a smooth $p$-adic formal scheme $X$ over $\operatorname{Spf}(A/I)$. Assume $X=\operatorname{Spf}(R)$ is affine and fix $i\geq0$.
theorems.statement: $H^i(R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L} A/I)\simeq\widehat{\Omega}^i_{R/(A/I)}\{-i\}$ canonically as $R$-modules.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Analytic adic and diamond étale sites
theorems.proof: The diamond associated with an analytic adic space over Zₚ has equivalent étale site under Scholze’s hypotheses. Comparison with quasi-pro-étale and v-cohomology for étale coefficients is a separate result in §14.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Finite étale covers and profinite Galois theory
theorems.proof: For a connected scheme X with geometric point x̄, the fibre functor induces an equivalence between finite étale X-schemes and finite discrete sets with continuous π₁(X,x̄)-action. This is a statement about finite covers; the full small étale topos of a general X is not thereby described.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: v and arc covers over Noetherian targets
theorems.proof: For a morphism of qcqs schemes with Noetherian target the v and arc covering tests agree, by reduction of the v test to discrete valuation rings. The reverse implication fails without the hypothesis, for example by the rank-two valuation construction in the valuative comparison.
refs: Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology, Proposition 2.6 and Corollary 2.9

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: K-theory and pro-cdh sheafification
theorems.proof: In the Noetherian finite-dimensional setting treated by Kelly–Saito, nonconnective K-theory is obtained by pro-cdh sheafification of connective K-theory. This application uses the thickenings in the generators and is distinct from ordinary cdh descent.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Small and big crystalline topoi
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided-power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and a scheme $X$ over $V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Use the size convention in Stacks Situation 60.7.5.
theorems.statement: The inclusion $\operatorname{Cris}(X/S)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{CRIS}(X/S)$ is fully faithful, continuous, cocontinuous and preserves finite nonempty limits. The induced map $i$ of topoi has a retraction $\pi$, with $\pi_* = i^{-1}$.
theorems.proof: The inclusion $\operatorname{Cris}(X/S)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{CRIS}(X/S)$ is fully faithful, continuous, cocontinuous and preserves finite nonempty limits. The induced map $i$ of topoi has a retraction $\pi$, with $\pi_* = i^{-1}$.
refs: Stacks 07I6 · divided power thickenings over X

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Crystalline to Zariski geometric morphism
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a divided-power scheme $(S,\mathcal I,\gamma)$ over $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and a scheme $X$ over $V(\mathcal I)$ on which $p$ is locally nilpotent. Use the size convention in Stacks Situation 60.7.5.
theorems.statement: The forgetful functor $(U,T,\delta)\mapsto U$ is continuous and cocontinuous and preserves products and fibre products. It induces $u_{X/S}:(X/S)_{\mathrm{cris}}\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}})$. Its direct image evaluates a crystalline sheaf on the trivial thickenings.
theorems.proof: The forgetful functor $(U,T,\delta)\mapsto U$ is continuous and cocontinuous and preserves products and fibre products. It induces $u_{X/S}:(X/S)_{\mathrm{cris}}\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}})$. Its direct image evaluates a crystalline sheaf on the trivial thickenings.
refs: Stacks 07IL · comparison with the Zariski site

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Forgetting the base prism
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a bounded prism $(A,I)$ and a smooth $p$-adic formal scheme $X$ over $\operatorname{Spf}(A/I)$. Use the bounded absolute site of the same $X$.
theorems.statement: Send a relative object $(A,I)\to(B,IB)$ with $\operatorname{Spf}(B/IB)\to X$ to the same prism over $X$, forgetting the map from $(A,I)$. Relative covering maps remain covers, since the prism ideal is unchanged. The arrow displays this functor on sites.
theorems.proof: Send a relative object $(A,I)\to(B,IB)$ with $\operatorname{Spf}(B/IB)\to X$ to the same prism over $X$, forgetting the map from $(A,I)$. Relative covering maps remain covers, since the prism ideal is unchanged. The arrow displays this functor on sites.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Definition 1.6, Remark 1.7 and Definition 4.1

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Global sections on the relative prismatic site
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a bounded prism $(A,I)$ and a smooth $p$-adic formal scheme $X$ over $\operatorname{Spf}(A/I)$.
theorems.statement: Take derived global sections of the structure sheaf $\mathcal O_\Delta$ on $(X/A)_\Delta$. On an object corresponding to $(B,IB)$ this sheaf has value $B$.
theorems.proof: Take derived global sections of the structure sheaf $\mathcal O_\Delta$ on $(X/A)_\Delta$. On an object corresponding to $(B,IB)$ this sheaf has value $B$.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Definition 4.1 and Theorem 1.8

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Prismatic to de Rham comparison
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a bounded prism $(A,I)$ and a smooth $p$-adic formal scheme $X$ over $\operatorname{Spf}(A/I)$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical comparison $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{dR}}(X/(A/I))\simeq R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)\widehat\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,\varphi_A} A/I$. The scalar map is Frobenius followed by reduction modulo $I$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical comparison $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{dR}}(X/(A/I))\simeq R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)\widehat\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,\varphi_A} A/I$. The scalar map is Frobenius followed by reduction modulo $I$.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorem 1.8(3) and Corollary 15.4

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Prismatic to étale comparison
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a prime $p$, a bounded prism $(A,I)$ and a smooth $p$-adic formal scheme $X$ over $\operatorname{Spf}(A/I)$. Assume $A$ is perfect, use the generic fibre $X_\eta$ of Theorem 9.1, and fix an integer $n\geq 1$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical comparison $R\Gamma_{\acute{e}t}(X_\eta,\mathbf Z/p^n)\simeq (R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)/p^n[1/I])^{\varphi=1}$. Reduction is derived, and the fixed points are taken in the derived sense.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical comparison $R\Gamma_{\acute{e}t}(X_\eta,\mathbf Z/p^n)\simeq (R\Gamma_\Delta(X/A)/p^n[1/I])^{\varphi=1}$. Reduction is derived, and the fixed points are taken in the derived sense.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Theorems 1.8(4) and 9.1

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Affine basis of the lfp big Zariski topos
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be an affine scheme. Use the Zariski site of $S$-schemes locally of finite presentation and a fixed size convention.
theorems.statement: Restriction to affine objects gives an equivalence of categories of sheaves. Every object admits an affine open cover, and an affine scheme locally of finite presentation over the affine base corresponds to a finitely presented algebra. The affine objects use the induced Zariski topology.
theorems.proof: Restriction to affine objects gives an equivalence of categories of sheaves. Every object admits an affine open cover, and an affine scheme locally of finite presentation over the affine base corresponds to a finitely presented algebra. The affine objects use the induced Zariski topology.
refs: Blechschmidt, Using the internal language of toposes, §15, parsimonious sites

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The parsimonious Zariski topos over the little topos
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be an affine scheme. Use the Zariski site of $S$-schemes locally of finite presentation and a fixed size convention.
theorems.statement: Use the lfp big Zariski topos, identified with the sheaves on the affine basis. Its canonical geometric morphism to the little topos has direct image given by restriction in the lfp site model. Its inverse image sends $\mathcal F$ to $T\mapsto\Gamma(T,f^{-1}\mathcal F)$ for $f:T\to S$.
theorems.proof: Use the lfp big Zariski topos, identified with the sheaves on the affine basis. Its canonical geometric morphism to the little topos has direct image given by restriction in the lfp site model. Its inverse image sends $\mathcal F$ to $T\mapsto\Gamma(T,f^{-1}\mathcal F)$ for $f:T\to S$.
refs: Blechschmidt, Using the internal language of toposes, §§15–16

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Qcqs schemes and their spectral spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme, and equip $|X|$ with its original Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated if and only if $|X|$ is spectral. Affine opens give a quasi-compact basis, sobriety holds for every scheme, and quasi-separatedness is equivalent to quasi-compactness of affine intersections.
theorems.proof: $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated if and only if $|X|$ is spectral. Affine opens give a quasi-compact basis, sobriety holds for every scheme, and quasi-separatedness is equivalent to quasi-compactness of affine intersections.
refs: Stacks 08YG · definition of a spectral space

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Formation of the patch topology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a spectral space with its given topology.
theorems.statement: The quasi-compact opens of $X$ and their complements generate the constructible topology. The identity $X_{\mathrm{patch}}\to X$ is continuous.
theorems.proof: The quasi-compact opens of $X$ and their complements generate the constructible topology. The identity $X_{\mathrm{patch}}\to X$ is continuous.
refs: Stacks 0901 · constructible topology of a spectral space

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The patch space is profinite
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be spectral and consider $X_{\mathrm{patch}}$, on the same underlying set.
theorems.statement: The patch topology is quasi-compact Hausdorff. Its generators are clopen and finite intersections form a clopen basis, so the patch space is totally disconnected and hence profinite.
theorems.proof: The patch topology is quasi-compact Hausdorff. Its generators are clopen and finite intersections form a clopen basis, so the patch space is totally disconnected and hence profinite.
refs: Stacks 0901 · constructible topology of a spectral space

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Coherent frames and their compact elements
theorems.hypotheses: Use coherent frames and frame homomorphisms preserving compact elements, or their opposite category of coherent locales. Use bounded distributive lattices and maps preserving the bounds and finite meets and joins.
theorems.statement: Taking the compact elements of a coherent frame and taking the frame of ideals of a bounded distributive lattice are inverse equivalences at the level of frames. Passing to locales reverses arrows.
theorems.proof: Taking the compact elements of a coherent frame and taking the frame of ideals of a bounded distributive lattice are inverse equivalences at the level of frames. Passing to locales reverses arrows.
refs: Banaschewski, Radical ideals and coherent frames, §1
Blechschmidt, Generalized spaces for constructive algebra
Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, Theorem 6

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Small and big étale topoi
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme. Use compatible choices of big and small sites as in Stacks Remark 34.11.1.
theorems.statement: The inclusion of the small site induces $i:X_{\acute{e}t}\to(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_{\acute{e}t}$ on topoi. There is a retraction $\pi$ with $\pi\circ i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\pi_*=i^{-1}$.
theorems.proof: The inclusion of the small site induces $i:X_{\acute{e}t}\to(\mathrm{Sch}/X)_{\acute{e}t}$ on topoi. There is a retraction $\pi$ with $\pi\circ i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\pi_*=i^{-1}$.
refs: Stacks 021G · Lemma 34.4.14, small and big étale sites

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Small étale to small Zariski
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme. Use compatible choices of big and small sites as in Stacks Remark 34.11.1.
theorems.statement: The inclusion of open immersions into étale objects induces the geometric morphism $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute{e}t})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}})$. Its direct image is restriction to the opens of $X$.
theorems.proof: The inclusion of open immersions into étale objects induces the geometric morphism $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute{e}t})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}})$. Its direct image is restriction to the opens of $X$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Big étale to big Zariski
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme. Use compatible choices of big and small sites as in Stacks Remark 34.11.1.
theorems.statement: The identity on the chosen underlying category induces the geometric morphism from the big étale topos to the big Zariski topos. A Zariski covering is an étale covering.
theorems.proof: The identity on the chosen underlying category induces the geometric morphism from the big étale topos to the big Zariski topos. A Zariski covering is an étale covering.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Big fppf to big étale
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme. Use compatible choices of big and small sites as in Stacks Remark 34.11.1.
theorems.statement: The identity on the common underlying category induces the geometric morphism from the big fppf topos to the big étale topos. Every étale covering is fppf.
theorems.proof: The identity on the common underlying category induces the geometric morphism from the big fppf topos to the big étale topos. Every étale covering is fppf.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Pro-étale to small étale
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme. Use compatible small étale and pro-étale sites as in Stacks §61.19.
theorems.statement: Inclusion of the étale objects induces $\epsilon:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute{e}t})$. The inverse image $\epsilon^{-1}$ is fully faithful.
theorems.proof: Inclusion of the étale objects induces $\epsilon:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\acute{e}t})$. The inverse image $\epsilon^{-1}$ is fully faithful.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Étale and pro-étale cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\epsilon$ the comparison of small sites. Take an abelian étale sheaf $\mathcal F$ or $K\in D^+(X_{\acute{e}t})$.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison is $R\Gamma(X_{\acute{e}t},K)\simeq R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\epsilon^{-1}K)$. In particular the pullback preserves cohomology in every degree for $\mathcal F$.
theorems.proof: The canonical comparison is $R\Gamma(X_{\acute{e}t},K)\simeq R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\epsilon^{-1}K)$. In particular the pullback preserves cohomology in every degree for $\mathcal F$.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Prismatic to formal étale topos
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a bounded prism $(A,I)$ and a smooth $p$-adic formal scheme $X$ over $\operatorname{Spf}(A/I)$. Use the formal small étale site in Construction 4.4.
theorems.statement: The quotient $(B,IB)\mapsto\operatorname{Spf}(B/IB)$ gives a cocontinuous functor to the big formal étale site. Composing the induced geometric morphism with the comparison to the small formal étale topos gives $\nu_X$. Over $U\to X$, the direct image of $\mathcal F$ is the space of sections over $(U/A)_\Delta$.
theorems.proof: The quotient $(B,IB)\mapsto\operatorname{Spf}(B/IB)$ gives a cocontinuous functor to the big formal étale site. Composing the induced geometric morphism with the comparison to the small formal étale topos gives $\nu_X$. Over $U\to X$, the direct image of $\mathcal F$ is the space of sections over $(U/A)_\Delta$.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Construction 4.4
Stacks 00XO · geometric morphism from a cocontinuous functor

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Formal étale site and the special fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a $p$-adic formal scheme and $X_0=X\bmod p$. Compare adic étale formal schemes over $X$ with étale schemes over $X_0$.
theorems.statement: Reduction to $X_0$ yields an equivalence of small étale sites. Étale objects lift uniquely up to unique isomorphism through the successive nilpotent thickenings $X\bmod p^n$, and these lifts form the formal étale object.
theorems.proof: Reduction to $X_0$ yields an equivalence of small étale sites. Étale objects lift uniquely up to unique isomorphism through the successive nilpotent thickenings $X\bmod p^n$, and these lifts form the formal étale object.
refs: Stacks 0DE9 · §87.34, the small étale site of a formal algebraic space
Stacks 04DZ · topological invariance of the étale site
Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Construction 4.4

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Little Zariski and localic presentations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme and take the locale whose frame is the opens of its Zariski space.
theorems.statement: There is an equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal O(|X|))$. Both sides impose the sheaf condition for open covers. If $X$ is qcqs, the locale of opens is coherent.
theorems.proof: There is an equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal O(|X|))$. Both sides impose the sheaf condition for open covers. If $X$ is qcqs, the locale of opens is coherent.
refs: Stacks 020X · small Zariski site and ordinary sheaves
Blechschmidt, Generalized spaces for constructive algebra

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: From covering families to covering sieves
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site specified by covering families satisfying the isomorphism, composition and base-change axioms.
theorems.statement: A sieve is covering precisely when it contains the sieve generated by some covering family. The resulting Grothendieck topology has the same sheaves as the covering-family presentation.
theorems.proof: The axioms on the families give the maximal-sieve, pullback and local-character axioms. A matching family on a cover extends to its generated sieve by compatibility on the pullbacks. Uniqueness and existence on a larger covering sieve can then be tested on a contained covering family and its pullbacks.
refs: Stacks 00ZC · covering families give a topology

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Sheafification detects covering sieves
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a topology $J$ on $\mathcal C$ and a sieve $S\subseteq h_U$ on an object $U$.
theorems.statement: $S\in J(U)$ if and only if $S^\#\to h_U^\#$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Sheafification preserves the monomorphism. For a covering sieve the local sections over the arrows of $S$ give the lift of $\operatorname{id}_U$ needed for surjectivity. Conversely a lift of $\operatorname{id}_U$ is represented locally by sections of $S$ after refinement, which gives a covering sieve contained in $S$.
refs: Stacks 00ZO · covering sieve detected by sheafification

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Recovering a topology from its sheaves
theorems.hypotheses: Let $J$ and $J'$ be Grothendieck topologies on the same category $\mathcal C$, with the same ambient presheaf category.
theorems.statement: $J=J'$ if and only if $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J)$ and $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J')$ are the same full subcategory of presheaves.
theorems.proof: A full subcategory of sheaves with its inclusion determines the left adjoint up to natural isomorphism. The sheafification criterion then recovers the covering sieves from that adjunction.
refs: Stacks 00ZP · topology determined by sheaves in presheaves

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Finite-limit preservation by sheafification
theorems.hypotheses: Let the presheaves and sheaves be set-valued on a site.
theorems.statement: The sheafification functor preserves finite limits and all small colimits.
theorems.proof: The plus construction uses directed colimits over refinements. Finite limits in sets commute with these colimits and with the limits imposing compatibility on matching families. Applying plus twice gives preservation of finite limits. The adjunction gives preservation of colimits.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Comparison lemma for sites
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous and cocontinuous. Require that two arrows with the same image under $u$ agree after a cover of their common source, and that an arrow $u(U')\to u(U)$ locally lifts after a cover of $U'$ in $\mathcal C$. Require every object of $\mathcal D$ to have a cover by objects in the image of $u$.
theorems.statement: The morphism $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ obtained from the cocontinuous functor $u$ is an equivalence.
theorems.proof: Local lifting and equality of arrows identify the sheafified morphism data on image objects. The covering condition then reconstructs each sheaf on the target from those local data by descent.
refs: Stacks 03A0 · comparison lemma with local fullness, faithfulness and cover density

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Subcanonical presentation by sheafified representables
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C'$ be a small full subcategory of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ containing the sheafified representables $h_U^\#$ and closed under fibre products in the sheaf category.
theorems.statement: The families in $\mathcal C'$ with epimorphic coproduct map form a subcanonical site presentation. The functor $U\mapsto h_U^\#$ induces $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')$.
theorems.proof: Epimorphisms of sheaves are effective and stable under pullback, so representables satisfy descent for the specified families. The original covers induce such epimorphisms, and the $h_U^\#$ generate the sheaf category. The resulting functor satisfies the site comparison hypotheses.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Conservative stalks detect finite limits and colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a conservative family of points of a site.
theorems.statement: Stalks jointly detect monomorphisms, epimorphisms, equality of morphisms, and limiting and colimiting cones for finite diagrams.
theorems.proof: Inverse images of points preserve finite limits and colimits. Compare a cone to the actual limit or colimit and use conservativity on the comparison map. For monomorphisms and epimorphisms one can test the diagonal and codiagonal, respectively. An equalizer detects equality of maps.
refs: Stacks 00YL · exactness and comparison at stalks

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Geometric stalks on small and big étale sites
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme, with the big site formed in a fixed size convention.
theorems.statement: The geometric points of $S$ give a conservative family for the small étale site. On the big étale site use the geometric points of all objects $T\to S$, evaluating the stalk after restriction to $T_{\text{ét}}$. Exactness of sequences of abelian sheaves on the small site is equivalent to exactness at the geometric stalks.
theorems.proof: A stalk is the filtered colimit over pointed étale neighbourhoods. A germ that lifts or vanishes does so after shrinking such a neighbourhood. Doing this above every point gives the covering family that witnesses the local sheaf condition for surjectivity or injectivity. On the big site these tests are made object by object.
refs: Stacks 040S · enough points of the small and big étale sites

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Étale structure sheaf stalk
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\bar s$ be a geometric point of a scheme $S$ lying over $s$, and take the separable algebraic closure of $\kappa(s)$ inside $\kappa(\bar s)$.
theorems.statement: The stalk $(\mathcal O_S)_{\bar s}$ on $S_{\text{ét}}$ identifies canonically with the strict henselization of $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ for that choice of separable closure.
theorems.proof: The filtered colimit of local rings of pointed étale neighbourhoods is the construction of the strict henselization with this residue field.
refs: Stacks 04HX · étale stalk as strict henselization

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Proper base change in étale cohomology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes and $g:Y'\to Y$ any morphism of schemes. Put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ and let $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$ be the projections. Let $F$ be an abelian torsion sheaf on $X_{\text{ét}}$.
theorems.statement: The base-change map $g^{-1}Rf_*F\to Rf'_*((g')^{-1}F)$ on $Y'_{\text{ét}}$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Reduce to $\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ and then test over strictly henselian local bases. For $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$-module sheaves with $\ell$ prime, restrictions of injectives to the closed fibre are acyclic for global sections. Computing by this resolution gives the fibre comparison, and dévissage and filtered colimits give the torsion assertion.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Weakly contractible pro-étale covers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be any scheme. Work in the small pro-étale site of $S$, the big pro-étale site over $S$, or the global big pro-étale site in the chosen size convention.
theorems.statement: Each object $U$ admits a singleton covering $\{V\to U\}$ by a weakly contractible object. When $U$ is quasi-compact, $V$ can be chosen affine. The affine versions of the sites admit covering families by affine quasi-compact weakly contractible objects.
theorems.proof: The construction gives weakly contractible affine covers of affine charts. A disjoint union of weakly contractible objects is weakly contractible, since evaluation on it is a product of evaluations on the components.
refs: Stacks 0990 · enough affine quasi-compact weakly contractible objects

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Cohomology on a weakly contractible object
theorems.hypotheses: Let $U$ be weakly contractible in a site $\mathcal C$. Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C$.
theorems.statement: Evaluation at $U$ is exact on abelian sheaves, so $H^i(U,F)=0$ for $i>0$. Every torsor for a sheaf of groups has a section over $U$.
theorems.proof: Evaluation preserves kernels, and weak contractibility makes evaluation of sheaf epimorphisms surjective. A torsor is locally nonempty, so its map to the terminal sheaf is epimorphic and lifts the unique section over the object.
refs: Stacks 0946 · acyclicity and sections of torsors

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Locally constant finitely presented coefficients
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\Lambda$ be a ring, and use the natural morphism $\epsilon:X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}\to X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ of small topoi.
theorems.statement: The functor $\epsilon^{-1}$ gives an equivalence between locally constant sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules of finite presentation on the two topoi.
theorems.proof: The inverse image is fully faithful. On an open piece where the fibre module has fixed isomorphism type $M$, the sheaf of trivializations is a torsor under the constant sheaf $\operatorname{Aut}_{\Lambda}(M)$ by finite presentation. Comparison of these torsors gives étale-local trivializations.
refs: Stacks 099Y · étale and pro-étale comparison for locally constant finitely presented modules

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Scheme and algebraic-space objects in the étale site
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be an algebraic space. Compare the small étale site using scheme objects over $X$ with the version using algebraic-space objects over $X$.
theorems.statement: The inclusion of the scheme objects induces an equivalence of topoi.
theorems.proof: The inclusion is fully faithful and continuous. Every algebraic-space object admits an étale cover by a scheme, and such refinements also yield cocontinuity. Apply the comparison lemma.
refs: Stacks 03G1 · comparison of the two étale sites of an algebraic space

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Affine presentation of the big fppf topos
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ belong to the chosen big fppf site of schemes.
theorems.statement: The inclusion $(\mathrm{Aff}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}\to(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ induces an equivalence of topoi.
theorems.proof: Every object has an affine open covering. For an affine target each fppf cover can be refined by a finite standard affine fppf cover. Together with full faithfulness these are the hypotheses of the comparison lemma.
refs: Stacks 021V · big and big affine fppf topoi

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Finite sober inverse limits characterize spectral spaces
theorems.hypotheses: Let the limit be taken in topological spaces over a directed inverse system.
theorems.statement: A space is spectral if and only if it can be presented as an inverse limit of finite sober spaces.
theorems.proof: A spectral space embeds in a product of Sierpiński spaces using its quasi-compact opens, with patch-closed image. Its projections to finite coordinate sets give finite sober spaces. Patch compactness identifies the image with the compatible tuples in these projections, and the finite-coordinate opens recover the spectral topology. Conversely, directed limits of finite sober spaces are spectral.
refs: Stacks 09XW · embedding in a product of Sierpiński spaces
Stacks 09XX · characterization by inverse limits of finite sober spaces

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Criterion for a subcanonical topology
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$. Let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on $\mathcal C$, and order topologies by inclusion of covering sieves.
theorems.statement: $J$ is subcanonical if and only if $J\subseteq J_{\mathrm{can}}$. One direction is maximality. Conversely, a representable sheaf for $J_{\mathrm{can}}$ satisfies the sheaf condition on every $J$-covering sieve.
theorems.proof: $J$ is subcanonical if and only if $J\subseteq J_{\mathrm{can}}$. One direction is maximality. Conversely, a representable sheaf for $J_{\mathrm{can}}$ satisfies the sheaf condition on every $J$-covering sieve.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: The canonical topology is subcanonical
theorems.hypotheses: Fix a small category $\mathcal C$ and use its canonical topology $J_{\mathrm{can}}$.
theorems.statement: Every representable presheaf on $\mathcal C$ is a $J_{\mathrm{can}}$-sheaf. Thus the canonical topology itself satisfies the predicate of subcanonicality.
theorems.proof: Every representable presheaf on $\mathcal C$ is a $J_{\mathrm{can}}$-sheaf. Thus the canonical topology itself satisfies the predicate of subcanonicality.
refs: Stacks 00ZA · definition of the canonical topology

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Localize at ∞-connective morphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal X$ be an ∞-topos.
theorems.statement: The ∞-connective maps are stable under pullback and form a strongly saturated class of small generation. Their localization is accessible and left exact; its target $\mathcal X^\wedge$ is again an ∞-topos.
theorems.proof: The ∞-connective maps are stable under pullback and form a strongly saturated class of small generation. Their localization is accessible and left exact; its target $\mathcal X^\wedge$ is again an ∞-topos.
refs: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 6.5.2.8 and following construction

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Hypercompletion produces a hypercomplete ∞-topos
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal X$ be an ∞-topos.
theorems.statement: The ∞-topos $\mathcal X^\wedge$ is hypercomplete. The original $\mathcal X$ is hypercomplete precisely when the localization functor is an equivalence.
theorems.proof: The ∞-topos $\mathcal X^\wedge$ is hypercomplete. The original $\mathcal X$ is hypercomplete precisely when the localization functor is an equivalence.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Objects retained by hypercompletion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $Z$ be an object of an ∞-topos $\mathcal X$.
theorems.statement: $Z$ is hypercomplete if and only if it is in the essential image of $\mathcal X^\wedge\hookrightarrow\mathcal X$; equivalently its localization unit is an equivalence.
theorems.proof: $Z$ is hypercomplete if and only if it is in the essential image of $\mathcal X^\wedge\hookrightarrow\mathcal X$; equivalently its localization unit is an equivalence.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Criterion by effectivity in all slices
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal X$ be an ∞-topos.
theorems.statement: $\mathcal X$ is hypercomplete if and only if, for every object $V$ of $\mathcal X$, every hypercover of $V$ in the slice $\mathcal X_{/V}$ is effective.
theorems.proof: $\mathcal X$ is hypercomplete if and only if, for every object $V$ of $\mathcal X$, every hypercover of $V$ in the slice $\mathcal X_{/V}$ is effective.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: An effective hypercover is a hypercover
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal X$ be an ∞-topos and let $V\in\mathcal X$.
theorems.statement: Effectivity adds the colimit condition to the degreewise effective epimorphism conditions.
theorems.proof: Effectivity adds the colimit condition to the degreewise effective epimorphism conditions.

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: A bounded prism is a prism
theorems.hypotheses: Work at a fixed prime p.
theorems.statement: Boundedness is an extra uniform annihilation condition on the p-power torsion of the quotient; all prism axioms remain required.
theorems.proof: Boundedness is an extra uniform annihilation condition on the p-power torsion of the quotient; all prism axioms remain required.
refs: Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Definition 1.1

theorems.subject: site
theorems.name: Pass to the opposite category
theorems.hypotheses: Take the category of frames with homomorphisms preserving finite meets and arbitrary joins.
theorems.statement: The category $\mathrm{Loc}$ is $\mathrm{Frm}^{\mathrm{op}}$. The object assignment is unchanged and each morphism is reversed.
theorems.proof: The category $\mathrm{Loc}$ is $\mathrm{Frm}^{\mathrm{op}}$. The object assignment is unchanged and each morphism is reversed.
refs: Banaschewski, Radical ideals and coherent frames, §1

theorems.subject: scheme
theorems.name: Representability of the Grassmannian functor
theorems.hypotheses: Fix integers $0<k<n$. For each scheme $S$, let $G(k,n)(S)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of locally free rank $n-k$ quotients of $\mathcal O_S^{\oplus n}$, with pullback on morphisms.
theorems.statement: There exists a scheme $\mathbf G(k,n)$ and a natural isomorphism $G(k,n)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(-,\mathbf G(k,n))$.
theorems.proof: The quotient functor is a Zariski sheaf. For each choice of n−k coordinates, the locus on which their images are a basis is represented by affine k(n−k)-space. These open subfunctors cover the functor.
refs: Grassmannian.info · classification over the classical homogeneous setting

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Localization of regular local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a regular local ring and let p be a prime ideal of R.
theorems.statement: The localization of R at p is regular local.
theorems.proof: The theorem follows from the local homological characterization and localization of a finite resolution.
refs: Stacks 0AFS · localizations of regular local rings

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Noetherianity under quotient, localization and finite type
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Choose an ideal I, a multiplicative subset S, or a finite type R-algebra A.
theorems.statement: The quotient R/I, the localization of R at S, and the algebra A are Noetherian.
theorems.proof: Every ideal in a quotient or localization comes from an ideal of the original ring. For finite type, apply the Hilbert basis theorem and pass to a quotient.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite type over a Jacobson ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be Jacobson and let A be a finite type R-algebra.
theorems.statement: The ring A is Jacobson. Each maximal ideal of A contracts to a maximal ideal of R and induces a finite extension of residue fields.
theorems.proof: Apply the finite type Jacobson theorem to the ring map and its quotient by a maximal ideal of A.
refs: Stacks 00GB · finite type over a Jacobson ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Normality under localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be normal and S be a multiplicative subset of R.
theorems.statement: The localization of R at S is normal.
theorems.proof: A prime of the localization corresponds to a prime of R disjoint from S, and the subsequent prime localizations are canonically isomorphic.
refs: Stacks 037C · localization of a normal ring

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Regular parameters are a regular sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a regular local ring of dimension d and choose a regular system of parameters.
theorems.statement: The chosen tuple is a regular sequence. The quotient by its first c terms is regular local of dimension d−c for every integer c between zero and d.
theorems.proof: Regularity gives a domain and hence each nonzero parameter is a nonzerodivisor on the relevant regular local quotient.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Zero-dimensional algebras of finite type over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let k be a field and A a nonzero finite type k-algebra.
theorems.statement: Dimension zero, finite prime spectrum, finite set of maximal ideals, finite dimension as a k-vector space, and Artinianness are equivalent.
theorems.proof: Noetherianity and the Jacobson property are available by finite type over a field. Use the dimension-zero characterization for this scope.
refs: Stacks 0ALW · finite type algebra with finitely many primes

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Polynomial algebras over a normal ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a normal ring and choose any set of polynomial indeterminates.
theorems.statement: The polynomial ring over R in those indeterminates is normal.
theorems.proof: For finitely many indeterminates, use the polynomial normality criterion. For an arbitrary set, take the filtered colimit over the finite subsets.
refs: Stacks 037D · filtered colimits of normal rings

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Finite type and localization preserve excellence
theorems.hypotheses: Let A be a finite type algebra over a quasi-excellent or excellent ring R. Let S be a multiplicative subset of A.
theorems.statement: The localization of A at S is quasi-excellent or excellent, respectively.
theorems.proof: Use the stability of G-rings and J-2 under the stated operations, and of universal catenarity in the excellent case.
refs: Stacks 07QU · permanence of quasi-excellence and excellence

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Noetherian valuation rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let R be a valuation ring.
theorems.statement: The ring R is Noetherian exactly when R is a field or a discrete valuation ring.
theorems.proof: In a Noetherian valuation ring every ideal is principal. If it is not a field, a generator of the maximal ideal yields the discrete valuation.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Absolute and relative complete intersections over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let k be a field and S be a finite type k-algebra.
theorems.statement: A prime localization of S is a complete intersection in the completion sense precisely when it is a complete intersection over k. Consequently the absolute and k-relative local complete intersection conditions agree for S.
theorems.proof: Use the comparison of the completion criterion and the regular-sequence presentation over a field.
refs: Stacks 09Q6 · agreement of complete intersection notions
Stacks 00SD · complete intersection over a field

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Exactness of module localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring, $U\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset, and $L\to M\to N$ an exact sequence of $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: The localized sequence $U^{-1}L\to U^{-1}M\to U^{-1}N$ is exact.
theorems.proof: An element sent to zero in a localization is killed by a denominator. Clearing such a denominator reduces exactness in the middle to exactness before localization.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Flatness under base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ be any ring map and $M$ an $R$-module. Let $M'=R'\otimes_R M$.
theorems.statement: If $M$ is flat over $R$, then $M'$ is flat over $R'$. If $M$ is faithfully flat over $R$, then $M'$ is faithfully flat over $R'$.
theorems.proof: On $R'$-modules the functor $M'\otimes_{R'}-$ identifies with $M\otimes_R-$. This transfers preservation of exactness and, in the faithful case, reflection of exactness.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of module flatness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ be faithfully flat and $M$ an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: $M$ is flat over $R$ if and only if $R'\otimes_R M$ is flat over $R'$.
theorems.proof: Apply base change to a sequence obtained by tensoring an injection with $M$. Faithfully flat base change detects the vanishing of its kernel.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of module finiteness and presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ be faithfully flat, and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: Finite generation of $M$ over $R$ is equivalent to finite generation of $R'\otimes_R M$ over $R'$. The analogous equivalence holds for finite presentation.
theorems.proof: Choose finitely many elements of $M$ whose scalar extensions generate. Faithful flatness detects surjectivity. For finite presentation apply the finite-generation argument to the kernel of a finite free surjection.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of finite projective modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ be faithfully flat and $M$ an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: $M$ is finite projective over $R$ if and only if $R'\otimes_R M$ is finite projective over $R'$.
theorems.proof: Combine descent of finite presentation and flatness with the finite-projective criterion.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Support as a vanishing set
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ a finite $R$-module.
theorems.statement: $\operatorname{Supp}_R(M)=V(\operatorname{Ann}_R(M))$.
theorems.proof: If a localization of the module vanishes, each generator is killed by some element outside the prime. The product kills the whole module and remains outside the prime.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Computing depth using Ext
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring and $M$ a nonzero finite $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The depth with respect to $\mathfrak m$ is the least nonnegative integer $i$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(R/\mathfrak m,M)\ne 0$.
theorems.proof: Start in degree zero with the criterion for an element annihilated by the ideal. The exact sequence for quotienting by a regular element of the ideal reduces the remaining degrees by one.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Fixed local rank via Fitting ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite $R$-module and fix a nonnegative integer $r$.
theorems.statement: $M$ is finite locally free of rank $r$ if and only if $\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(M)=0$ and $\operatorname{Fit}_r(M)=R$.
theorems.proof: The minors test the presentation on localizations at primes. In a local presentation with a minimal generating family, the two conditions give precisely the stated free rank.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Descent of regularity conditions for ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be faithfully flat and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal.
theorems.statement: If $IB$ is Koszul-regular, $H_1$-regular, or quasi-regular in $B$, respectively, then $I$ has the corresponding property in $A$.
theorems.proof: Finite generation descends. Locally choose a minimal generating sequence and test the relevant homology or associated graded map by faithfully flat base change.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of algebra finiteness and presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $R\to R'$ faithfully flat. Put $S'=R'\otimes_R S$.
theorems.statement: $R\to S$ has finite type if and only if $R'\to S'$ has finite type. The analogous equivalence holds for finite presentation.
theorems.proof: Descend algebra generators using faithful flatness. For finite presentation, apply descent for finite modules to the defining ideal after choosing a finite polynomial presentation.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of finite ring maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and $S\to T$ both be finite.
theorems.statement: The composite $R\to T$ is finite.
theorems.proof: Products of module generators for the two extensions generate the target module over the initial ring.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of integral ring maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and $S\to T$ both be integral.
theorems.statement: The composite $R\to T$ is integral.
theorems.proof: The coefficients of an integral equation lie in a finite intermediate algebra over the initial ring. Adjoining the root produces a further finite extension.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Faithfully flat descent of syntomicity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $R\to R'$ faithfully flat. Put $S'=R'\otimes_R S$.
theorems.statement: $R\to S$ is syntomic if and only if $R'\to S'$ is syntomic.
theorems.proof: Flatness and finite presentation descend faithfully flatly, and the fibre condition is invariant under the corresponding residue field extensions.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Smoothness under base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be smooth and $R\to R'$ any ring map.
theorems.statement: $R'\to R'\otimes_R S$ is smooth.
theorems.proof: Base change standard smooth presentations on the target cover. The Jacobian minor remains invertible.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Étale composition and base change
theorems.hypotheses: Use commutative rings with unit. In the composition statement both maps are étale. In the base change statement the map along which one base changes is arbitrary.
theorems.statement: Composites and base changes of étale maps are étale.
theorems.proof: Finite presentation has both permanence properties. For formal étaleness, use its existence and uniqueness of lifts, and the universal property of tensor products.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Classification of étale algebras over a field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a $k$-algebra.
theorems.statement: $k\to S$ is étale if and only if $S$ is a finite product of finite separable field extensions of $k$. The empty product gives the zero algebra.
theorems.proof: An étale algebra has finite-dimensional fibre over the unique point of the field, and its local factors are separable fields. Conversely, the product of finitely many such field extensions is étale.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Quasi-finiteness under base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be of finite type, let $R\to R'$ be arbitrary, and put $S'=R'\otimes_R S$.
theorems.statement: Quasi-finiteness ascends to $R'\to S'$. It also descends if $\operatorname{Spec}(R')\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: The residue-field extension at a base prime preserves and reflects whether its fibre algebra has finite dimension.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat map and flat target module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and view $S$ as an $R$-module through it.
theorems.statement: The ring map is flat if and only if this module is flat.
theorems.proof: This equivalence is the definition. It relates the map to its associated target module.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Faithfully flat map and faithfully flat target module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and view $S$ as an $R$-module through it.
theorems.statement: The ring map is faithfully flat if and only if this module is faithfully flat.
theorems.proof: This equivalence is the definition. It relates the map to its associated target module.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite map and finite target module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and view $S$ as an $R$-module through it.
theorems.statement: The ring map is finite if and only if this module is finitely generated.
theorems.proof: This equivalence is the definition of a finite ring map.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Pure ideal and flat quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal in the ring $R$.
theorems.statement: $I$ is pure if and only if $R/I$ is flat as an $R$-module, equivalently if $R\to R/I$ is flat.
theorems.proof: Apply the definitions to the specific quotient module and quotient map.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Modules over a field have bases
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field and $V$ an $F$-module.
theorems.statement: The module $V$ is free over $F$.
theorems.proof: A maximal linearly independent subset of $V$ exists by Zorn’s lemma. Any vector outside its span would enlarge it.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Exact sequences of vector spaces split
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field and $0\to U\to V\to W\to 0$ a short exact sequence of $F$-modules.
theorems.statement: There is an $F$-linear section $W\to V$ of the quotient map.
theorems.proof: Lift an $F$-basis of $W$ to $V$ and extend the resulting map linearly.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: A field map to a nonzero ring is injective
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field, $R$ a nonzero ring, and $f:F\to R$ a unital ring map.
theorems.statement: The map $f$ is injective.
theorems.proof: The kernel is an ideal of the field. It cannot contain $1$ because the target is nonzero and the map is unital.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Characteristic is zero or prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field and use its canonical map from $\mathbf Z$.
theorems.statement: Exactly one of these cases holds. In characteristic zero the prime subfield is $\mathbf Q$. In characteristic $p>0$ the prime subfield is $\mathbf F_p$.
theorems.proof: The kernel of $\mathbf Z\to F$ is prime because $F$ is an integral domain. The prime ideals of $\mathbf Z$ give the two alternatives.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Perfect field criterion by characteristic
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field.
theorems.statement: The field is perfect if and only if its characteristic is zero or it has positive characteristic with surjective Frobenius.
theorems.proof: In positive characteristic a missing $p$th root gives an inseparable algebraic extension. If Frobenius is surjective then the purely inseparable tensor-product tests for general separability are automatic.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Classification of simple extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E=F(a)$ be a simple extension with specified generator $a$.
theorems.statement: If $a$ is transcendental, evaluation gives an isomorphism $F(T)\cong E$. If $a$ is algebraic, evaluation gives $F[T]/(P)\cong E$ for the minimal polynomial $P$ of $a$.
theorems.proof: Evaluation on $F[T]$ has zero kernel in the first case and the prime ideal generated by the minimal polynomial in the second.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Fraction field of an integral domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an integral domain.
theorems.statement: Its fraction field is the localization at the nonzero elements. Every injective ring map $A\to K$ into a field extends uniquely to a field map $\operatorname{Frac}(A)\to K$.
theorems.proof: Send $a/b$ to the image of $a$ times the inverse of the image of $b$. Injectivity ensures that these denominators are invertible, and multiplication and equality are well defined by cross multiplication.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Vector space dimension of a rational function field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $T$ be transcendental over the field $F$.
theorems.statement: The extension $F(T)/F$ is infinite-dimensional. For an infinite field $F$ it has dimension $|F|$.
theorems.proof: The monomials give an infinite independent family. For each $a\in F$, the functions $1/(T-a)$ are linearly independent: clear the denominators in a finite relation and evaluate in turn at the corresponding values $a$. The number of rational functions is at most $|F|$ when $F$ is infinite.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Field of meromorphic functions on a Riemann surface
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a connected Riemann surface.
theorems.statement: Meromorphic functions on $X$ form a field containing $\mathbf C$ via the constant functions. On the Riemann sphere this is $\mathbf C(T)$.
theorems.proof: A nonzero meromorphic function on a connected surface has a meromorphic inverse. On the sphere, subtract principal parts at its finitely many poles to obtain a constant holomorphic function.
refs: Stacks 09FY · constant functions give the extension of $\mathbf C$

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Function field of a compact Riemann surface
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a compact connected Riemann surface and $f$ a nonconstant meromorphic function on $X$.
theorems.statement: The field $\mathbf C(X)$ is algebraic over $\mathbf C(f)$. It has transcendence degree one over $\mathbf C$.
theorems.proof: A nonconstant meromorphic function defines a finite holomorphic map to the sphere. For a meromorphic function on the source, the elementary symmetric functions in its values on the sheets define meromorphic coefficients on the sphere, giving an algebraic equation.
refs: Stacks 09IB · transcendence degree for the function field

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
theorems.name: Common extension of two fields over a base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ and $L/F$ be arbitrary field extensions.
theorems.statement: There is a field $M/F$ and injective $F$-maps from $E$ and $L$ to $M$.
theorems.proof: The tensor product $E\otimes_F L$ is nonzero. Quotient by a maximal ideal and use that unital maps from fields to the resulting field are injective.
refs: Stacks 09FU · field maps into nonzero rings

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Degree in a tower of field extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower of field extensions.
theorems.statement: $[L:F]=[L:E][E:F]$, with multiplication of cardinal numbers. If $L/F$ is finite, so are $L/E$ and $E/F$.
theorems.proof: Products of a basis of $L$ over $E$ with a basis of $E$ over $F$ form a basis of $L$ over $F$.
refs: Stacks 09G5 · finiteness over an intermediate field

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Algebraicity in towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be field extensions and let $a\in L$.
theorems.statement: If $a$ is algebraic over $F$ then it is algebraic over $E$. If $L/F$ is algebraic then $L/E$ is algebraic. If both $L/E$ and $E/F$ are algebraic then $L/F$ is algebraic.
theorems.proof: A polynomial with coefficients in $F$ is still a polynomial over $E$. For transitivity, the finitely many coefficients of a polynomial over $E$ belong to a finite extension of $F$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Cardinality of an algebraic extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic.
theorems.statement: The cardinality of $E$ is at most $\max(\aleph_0,|F|)$.
theorems.proof: There are at most this many nonzero polynomials in $F[T]$, and each has finitely many roots in $E$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Algebraic elements form a subfield
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be any field extension.
theorems.statement: The elements of $E$ algebraic over $F$ form the relative algebraic closure of $F$ in $E$.
theorems.proof: Any two such elements lie in a finite subextension, which also contains their sum, product and inverses when nonzero.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Intermediate subrings of algebraic extensions are fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic and $F\subseteq A\subseteq E$ an intermediate unital subring.
theorems.statement: The subring $A$ is a field.
theorems.proof: For nonzero $a\in A$, its minimal polynomial over $F$ has nonzero constant term. Dividing the polynomial relation by $a$ expresses $a^{-1}$ as an $F$-polynomial in $a$.

theorems.subject: field-map
theorems.name: Endomorphisms of algebraic extensions are automorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic and $u:E\to E$ a unital $F$-algebra map.
theorems.statement: The map $u$ is an $F$-automorphism.
theorems.proof: For every $a\in E$, the map permutes the finite set of roots in $E$ of the minimal polynomial of $a$ over $F$: injectivity gives a bijection on this set. Thus every $a$ is in the image.

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.name: Minimal polynomial and degree of a simple extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $a$ be algebraic over $F$ with minimal polynomial $P$ of degree $d$.
theorems.proof: Evaluation identifies $F(a)$ with $F[T]/(P)$ and the residue classes of $1,T,\dots,T^{d-1}$ form a basis.
refs: Stacks 09G7 · degree of a simple algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Existence and uniqueness of algebraic closures
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field.
theorems.statement: There exists an algebraic closure of $F$. Any two are isomorphic over $F$, generally by more than one isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The construction adjoins algebraic roots in stages. An $F$-embedding of one algebraic closure in another is surjective, since its image is algebraically closed and the larger field is algebraic over it.
refs: Stacks 09GU · embedding into an algebraic closure

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Embedding into an algebraic closure
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic and let $\overline F$ be an algebraic closure of $F$.
theorems.statement: There exists an $F$-embedding $E\hookrightarrow\overline F$.
theorems.proof: Order partial $F$-embeddings of intermediate fields by extension. At a maximal partial embedding, a root of the transported minimal polynomial extends the map unless the entire domain has been embedded.

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.name: Decomposition of an inseparable irreducible polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be an inseparable irreducible polynomial over a field $F$.
theorems.statement: The characteristic is $p>0$. There is a maximal power $q=p^r$ with $P(T)=Q(T^q)$, and $Q$ is irreducible and separable. The distinct roots of $P$ correspond to the distinct roots of $Q$ by the map $x\mapsto x^q$ in an algebraic closure.
theorems.proof: If the derivative is zero, all exponents with nonzero coefficient are multiples of $p$. Remove the largest common $p$-power from those exponents. The resulting derivative is nonzero and irreducibility descends to $Q$. Frobenius is bijective in the algebraic closure.
refs: Stacks 09H4 · the effect of Frobenius on the set of roots

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Algebraic separability in towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower of algebraic field extensions.
theorems.statement: Elements separable over $F$ are separable over $E$, and separability of $L/F$ gives separability of both $E/F$ and $L/E$. If $L/E$ and $E/F$ are separable, then $L/F$ is separable.
theorems.proof: Changing the base upward replaces a minimal polynomial by a divisor. For transitivity, pass to finite intermediate extensions containing the elements and coefficients in question, then use the embedding count.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Separable elements form a subfield
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be any field extension.
theorems.statement: The elements of $E$ separable over $F$ form a subfield containing $F$.
theorems.proof: Two separable elements generate a finite separable subextension by transitivity. This gives closure under the field operations.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Counting embeddings along a generating tower
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E=F(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ with each $a_i$ algebraic over $F$, and set $F_i=F(a_1,\dots,a_i)$. Let $P_i$ be the minimal polynomial of $a_i$ over $F_{i-1}$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline F$.
theorems.statement: At each step, after choosing an embedding of $F_{i-1}$, the image of $a_i$ can be any distinct root of the transported $P_i$. This gives $\prod_{i=1}^n\deg_s(P_i)$ embeddings of $E$ over $F$. Their number equals $[E:F]$ if every step is separable and is smaller if some step is inseparable.
theorems.proof: The universal property of the simple-extension presentation gives one lift per root. The number of roots of the transported polynomial is the separable degree. Compare the product with the tower law.
refs: Stacks 09H7 · bijection with tuples of roots
Stacks 09H9 · criterion for separably generated finite towers

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Independence of distinct multiplicative characters
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field and $G$ a monoid. Let $\chi_1,\dots,\chi_n:G\to(F,\cdot)$ be distinct monoid homomorphisms.
theorems.statement: These functions are linearly independent over $F$. In particular, distinct embeddings of an extension into $F$ are $F$-linearly independent as functions when their common domain and base are fixed.
theorems.proof: In a nontrivial linear relation of minimal support, compare the relation at $gh$ with the relation at $h$ multiplied by one of the character values at $g$. Choose $g$ on which two characters in the support differ. Subtraction gives a nonzero relation with smaller support.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: A nonzero power sum among distinct field elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be pairwise distinct elements of a field $F$, with $n\geq 1$.
theorems.statement: There is an integer $e\geq0$ for which $\sum_i a_i^e\ne0$.
theorems.proof: The functions $e\mapsto a_i^e$ are distinct characters of the additive monoid of nonnegative integers. Their sum, whose coefficients are all $1$, cannot vanish identically.

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
theorems.name: Splitting a finite separable extension after base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite separable, and let $L/F$ be a field extension with $L$ algebraically closed.
theorems.statement: The map $E\otimes_F L\to\prod_{\sigma:E\hookrightarrow L}L$ given by $a\otimes b\mapsto(\sigma(a)b)_\sigma$ is an isomorphism of $L$-algebras.
theorems.proof: The primitive element theorem writes $E$ as a polynomial quotient. The minimal polynomial splits into distinct linear factors over $L$, and the Chinese remainder theorem gives the product.

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.name: Irreducibility of a missing pth root polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ have characteristic $p>0$ and let $a\in F$ be an element outside $F^p$.
theorems.statement: The polynomial $X^p-a$ is irreducible in $F[X]$.
theorems.proof: In an algebraic closure it is $(X-b)^p$. A proper nonconstant monic factor of degree $d<p$ would have coefficient $-db$ in $F$, forcing $b\in F$.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Pure inseparability in towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower, and assume $L/E$ and $E/F$ are purely inseparable.
theorems.statement: The extension $L/F$ is purely inseparable.
theorems.proof: In characteristic $p>0$, apply first a $p$-power carrying an element from $L$ to $E$, then a further $p$-power carrying its image to $F$. In characteristic zero the two extensions are trivial.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Purely inseparable elements form a subfield
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be any field extension.
theorems.statement: The elements of $E$ purely inseparable over $F$ form a subfield containing $F$.
theorems.proof: For two such elements in positive characteristic, take a common exponent to send them to $F$ by the same Frobenius power, which respects the field operations. In characteristic zero the subfield is $F$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: A finite purely inseparable extension is built from pth roots
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite purely inseparable with characteristic $p>0$.
theorems.statement: There is a finite tower from $F$ to $E$ whose nontrivial steps have degree $p$ and are obtained by adjoining a $p$th root. Consequently $[E:F]$ is a power of $p$.
theorems.proof: If an element is outside the current field, take its penultimate $p$-power for a minimal exponent that puts a power into that field. This produces a degree-$p$ step by the missing-root criterion. Finite degree bounds the number of steps.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Canonical separable and purely inseparable factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic.
theorems.statement: There is a unique intermediate field $E_s$ such that $E_s/F$ is separable and $E/E_s$ is purely inseparable. It consists of the elements of $E$ separable over $F$.
theorems.proof: An inseparable minimal polynomial is a separable irreducible polynomial in a $p$-power of its variable. This sends each element into the separable subfield by some $p$-power. A separable and purely inseparable extension is trivial, which yields uniqueness.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Separable and inseparable degrees in towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower of algebraic extensions.
theorems.statement: $[L:F]_s=[L:E]_s[E:F]_s$ and $[L:F]_i=[L:E]_i[E:F]_i$. For finite extensions the separable degree is the number of embeddings into an algebraic closure.
theorems.proof: Use the separable-first factorization and the degrees in the resulting tower. For the finite embedding statement, an embedding of the separable part extends uniquely across the purely inseparable part.
refs: Stacks 09HJ · finite separable degree and embeddings

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Normality over an intermediate field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/F$ be normal and $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$.
theorems.statement: The extension $L/E$ is normal. If $L/F$ is Galois then $L/E$ is Galois.
theorems.proof: A minimal polynomial over $E$ divides a polynomial over $F$ that splits in $L$. The same divisor argument preserves separability.
refs: Stacks 09I2 · Galois extensions over intermediate fields

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Intersections of normal subextensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/F$ be algebraic and let $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ be a nonempty family of subextensions normal over $F$.
theorems.statement: Their intersection in $L$ is normal over $F$.
theorems.proof: For any element in the intersection, all the roots of its minimal polynomial over $F$ belong to each $E_i$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: The separable part of a normal extension is Galois
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be normal and let $E_s$ be its maximal separable subextension.
theorems.statement: The extension $E_s/F$ is Galois, and $E/E_s$ is purely inseparable and normal.
theorems.proof: Every conjugate of an element separable over $F$ is again separable over $F$. Normality of $E/F$ puts all the conjugates in $E$, hence in $E_s$. Normality over $E_s$ follows by passage to an intermediate field.

theorems.subject: field-extension
